It also says successors serve two-year terms, and any replacement for a vacancy serves only the rest of that term.

11689.s: This order extends diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Mission to the United States of America of the Commission of the European Communities. It also applies to certain officers of that mission in Washington who represent the Commission to the U.S. government, and to their families. They get the same privileges and immunities as diplomatic missions and diplomatic staff accredited to the United States, subject to the same conditions and obligations.

11687.s: This order lets the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Health, Education, and Welfare, and Transportation make regulations for the Survivor Benefit Plan without further presidential approval. The regulations must fit the law and be as uniform as practical, with some issued only after consulting the Secretary of Defense. They must include procedures for informing service members and, when required, their spouses about election choices, submitting elections and claims, making deposits, and fixing administrative problems.

11685.s: This order changes parts of two earlier executive orders on foreign assistance and foreign military sales. It updates which officials and sections are covered, revokes some old sections, and changes several legal references in the foreign assistance order. It also says the Secretary of the Treasury must consult with the Secretary of State when carrying out certain delegated foreign assistance functions.

11684.s: This order suspends a part of federal law that limited how many Navy and Marine Corps officers below the promotion zone could be recommended for promotion. It applies to Navy and Marine Corps officers and lasts until June 30, 1974.

11683.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 11677, except that the revocation does not affect violations that happened while it was in effect. It also keeps Executive Order No. 11533 and related export-control actions in force until they are amended, modified, or terminated by proper authority.

11682.s: This order lets the Department of the Treasury inspect certain tax returns when needed to administer the Economic Stabilization Act of 1970, as amended. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It affects tax returns covered by section 6103(a)(2) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954.

11681.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 5221 from 1929. That earlier order had set limits on non-official employment of officers or employees of the American Government.

11680.s: This order sets a line of Treasury Department officers who would act as Secretary of the Treasury if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are dead, resign, absent, or sick. It names the Under Secretary for Monetary Affairs, the Under Secretary or Counselor, the General Counsel, and then other assistant and deputy under secretaries in a set order. It also revokes a previous executive order on this same subject.

11679.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road Company and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, the company and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

11678.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness the power to use authority under a disaster loan law for disaster victims, without needing further approval from the President. It also lets the Director pass that authority to heads of executive branch agencies, with their consent, and let them pass it on to certain subordinates.

11677.s: This order keeps export controls in place even after the Export Administration Act of 1969 expired. It says the Commerce Department rules and related licenses, orders, and other actions stay in effect until changed or revoked. It also sets a maximum fine of $10,000 under one rule and says one civil penalty will not apply to violations under this order.

11676.s: The order creates an Office of National Narcotics Intelligence within the Department of Justice and gives it a director. That office must develop and maintain a national narcotics intelligence system and may gather information from federal, state, and local agencies. It may share narcotics intelligence with officials who have a legitimate official need for it, and federal agencies must help when requested and allowed by law.

11675.s: This order exempts John S. Patterson, a member of the Subversive Activities Control Board, from mandatory retirement for age. It lets him keep serving until August 10, 1976.

11674.s: This order changes Executive Order 11640 so the price controls it authorizes do not apply to raw agricultural products until after their first sale. It affects the prices charged for those farm products.

11673.s: This order redefines the Culebra Island Naval Defensive Sea Area to cover certain territorial waters around part of Culebra. It says the change applies to the waters between the extreme high-water mark and the three-mile marine boundary next to the described part of the island. It also says the order does not change the Culebra Island Naval Airspace Reservation or limit the Federal Aviation Administrator’s authority over that airspace.

11671.s: This order sets rules for federal committees that advise or help the government. It says departments and agencies must control how these committees are formed, approved, staffed, and kept open to the public. It also requires records, reporting, and limits on how long many committees may continue unless they are renewed.

11672.s: This order delegates to the Administrator of General Services the President’s authority under the Postal Reorganization Act to transfer or furnish property to the Postal Service. It says property transfers are generally to be reimbursed at fair market value, unless the Director of the Office of Management and Budget finds a different basis or no reimbursement is more fair or better serves the public interest. It also allows reimbursement to be made in cash, or in some cases with property, and lets agency heads require reimbursement for property they furnish to the Postal Service.

11670.s: This order changes part of the eastern boundary of the Gifford Pinchot National Forest and removes a tract of land from the Forest. It directs the Secretary of the Interior to take jurisdiction over that tract and administer it for the use and benefit of the Yakima Tribe of Indians as part of the reservation created by the 1855 treaty. Any earlier order or proclamation that conflicts with this change is superseded.

11669.s: This order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect to the memory of J. Edgar Hoover. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the United States and its territories, and to U.S. embassies, consular offices, and other facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11667.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Committee on the Environmental Merit Awards Program. The committee advises the President and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency on how to expand the program and on ways to recognize individuals or groups for local environmental accomplishments. The Environmental Protection Agency must provide administrative support, and committee members do not get pay from the United States, though they may receive travel expenses if allowed by law.

11668.s: The order directs the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to help create a new, non-governmental, not-for-profit National Center for Housing Management. The center is meant to help meet the nation’s housing management and training needs, especially for federally-assisted housing and low and moderate income residents. Federal departments and agencies are to cooperate with HUD and the center and may provide advice and financial support.

11666.s: This order says certain purchases do not have to follow a tax rule for the investment credit. It applies to articles costing no more than $500 and to agricultural implements, machinery, and equipment that the Secretary of the Treasury determines are free of duty under the tariff schedules. It applies to property bought under orders placed after August 15, 1971, and before December 20, 1971.

11664.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Penn Central Transportation Company and certain of its employees represented by the United Transportation Union. It also says that, unless the company and its employees agree otherwise, no change may be made in the conditions out of which the dispute arose during the stated period after the order and after the board reports to the President.

11665.s: This order directs that the flag of the United States be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for the memory of James F. Byrnes. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and throughout the United States and its territories and possessions, and to U.S. embassies, legations, consular offices, and other facilities abroad, including military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11662.s: This order changes a prior executive order to say "Disaster Relief Act of 1970, as amended" instead of "Disaster Relief Act of 1970." It also says any other order that refers to the Disaster Relief Act of 1970 will be treated as referring to the act as amended.

11661.s: This order revokes Executive Order 11260, which had amended an earlier order about coordinating federal education programs. It says Executive Order 11185 will be treated as still in effect as it was first issued, unless changed later.

11663.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain employees represented by the Sheet Metal Workers' International Association. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not make changes in the conditions out of which the disputes arose unless they agree to do so.

11660.s: This order continues the Pay Board and Price Commission and says their chairmen, acting with a majority vote, may take steps needed to help stabilize prices, rents, wages, and salaries. It also changes how members of the Board and Commission are appointed, including Senate consent rules and an exception for some members already serving. The order confirms and keeps in force earlier orders, regulations, circulars, and other actions unless changed or revoked by proper authority.

11659.s: This order establishes the Upper Mississippi River Basin Commission under the Water Resources Planning Act. Its jurisdiction covers parts of Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin within the Upper Mississippi River drainage basin. The commission includes a chairman, members from certain federal departments and agencies, members from those five states, and members from certain interstate agencies. It must provide for consultation with Indiana, Michigan, and South Dakota on matters that might affect water and related land resources in those states, and its chairman reports to the President through the Water Resources Council.

11658.s: This order establishes the Missouri River Basin Commission under the Water Resources Planning Act. The Commission covers Nebraska and parts of Colorado, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, North Dakota, South Dakota, and Wyoming within the Missouri River drainage basin. It includes a chairman, federal members, state members, and members from certain interstate agencies. The chairman must send matters involving the United States and Canada to the Water Resources Council, and report to the President through that council.

11657.s: This order exempts C. Everett Spangler, a member of the Federal Farm Credit Board, from compulsory retirement for age. It keeps him in that position until April 1, 1974.

11656.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1956 to 1972 open to inspection by the Select Committee on Crime in the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s study and investigation of crime affecting the United States and must follow Treasury rules.

11654.s: This order moves the Federal Fire Council from the General Services Administration to the Department of Commerce. The Council advises on protecting federal employees and property from fire, and the Secretary of Commerce or a designee will serve as its chairman. The Council may develop fire safety standards and procedures, review new construction plans when asked, study federal buildings and property, and keep records of fire losses on government property.

11655.s: This order allows the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1947 to 1972 during the Ninety-second Congress. The inspections must follow Treasury rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury. It affects taxpayers whose returns fall within those years.

11653.s: This order exempts Jack T. Stuart, a United States Marshal for the Southern District of Mississippi, from compulsory retirement for age. It lets him stay in that job until May 19, 1975.

11652.s: This order sets rules for classifying national security information as "Top Secret," "Secret," or "Confidential." It limits who in the executive branch can assign these classifications and says classified material must be downgraded or declassified when allowed. It also sets schedules for automatic declassification, with some exceptions for foreign government information, cryptography, intelligence sources or methods, certain foreign relations matters, and information that would put a person in immediate jeopardy.

11650.s: This order says certain tax returns under the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 may be open to inspection by certain classes of persons and by State and Federal Government establishments. It says this must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury and related amendments approved before and on this date.

11651.s: This order sets up a Committee for the Implementation of Textile Agreements to oversee all textile trade agreements. The committee can direct or recommend actions to carry out those agreements, and the Commissioner of Customs must take actions the committee recommends for textiles and textile products entering the United States. The Secretary of State must handle negotiations and communications with foreign governments about these textile trade agreements.

11649.s: This order sets rules for using the seals and coats of arms of the President and Vice President. It generally prohibits making, reproducing, selling, or buying them for resale, except in listed uses such as by the President or Vice President, in books and journals about seals or the Presidency, in libraries and museums, in archives, on monuments, in bona fide news content, or for other approved historical, educational, or newsworthy uses. It also bars using the seal or coat of arms on the covers of those books and publications.

11648.s: This order changes the rules for the White House Fellows program. It says the commission will set standards, take applications and nominations, and recommend outstanding young persons for the President to choose from, including regular members of the Armed Forces. It also says White House Fellows serve for 12 months in the White House staff, the Executive Office of the President, the Office of the Vice President, or offices of Cabinet members. Executive agencies must cooperate with the program, and the United States Civil Service Commission must provide administrative support and travel expenses as allowed by law.

11646.s: This order adds the Department of State to the Great Lakes Basin Commission. It also requires the Council and the Department of State to consult as appropriate on matters that relate to the International Joint Commission and the Great Lakes Fishery Commission. The order affects the Commission and the Department of State.

11647.s: This order creates a Federal Regional Council for each of the ten standard Federal regions. The councils are made up of regional officials from several federal agencies and are meant to help those agencies work together on grantmaking, program delivery, and coordination with governors, mayors, and local communities. It also creates an Under Secretaries Group for Regional Operations to set policy for the councils and help resolve policy issues.

11645.s: This order lets the Secretary of Transportation, or the Coast Guard Commandant under a delegation, prescribe regulations for the designation and leasing of rental housing. It says these regulations do not need approval or other action by the President, and if the Coast Guard operates as a service in the Navy, the Secretary of Navy is used instead of the Secretary of Transportation.

11644.s: This order directs federal agencies to set rules for where off-road vehicles may and may not be used on public lands. It requires them to issue operating conditions, mark permitted areas, share maps and other information, and set enforcement procedures. The rules are meant to protect land resources, public safety, and other uses of the land, and they do not apply to official use.

11643.s: This order restricts the use of chemical toxicants on Federal lands for killing predatory mammals or birds, and it also restricts toxicants that cause secondary poisoning when used to kill other mammals, birds, or reptiles. It says animal damage control programs on Federal lands must be carried out in a way that protects environmental quality and wildlife resources. Agency heads may allow emergency use only after a written finding that no other means will work and that the use is essential for human safety, protecting threatened wildlife, or preventing major damage to important natural resources.

11642.s: This order exempts A. Everette MacIntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. It extends that exemption until February 28, 1973.

11641.s: The order creates an Office for Drug Abuse Law Enforcement in the Department of Justice. It gives the office director a role advising the President and coordinating federal efforts on laws about illegal drug traffic and drug abuse prevention. Federal departments and agencies must help the director when requested, and the office is to work with state and local governments.

11640.s: This order continues the federal program to stabilize prices, rents, wages, and salaries. It keeps the Cost of Living Council, the Pay Board, and the Price Commission in place, and gives them authority to set and adjust limits and rules under the Economic Stabilization Act. It also requires people and businesses covered by the order to follow the price and wage limits, keep records, and make some records available for public inspection.

11638.s: This order raises the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It takes effect on January 1, 1972.

11639.s: This order directs executive agencies and military departments to set basic pay for covered federal employees using instructions from the United States Civil Service Commission. The Commission must issue those instructions and keep pay adjustments in line with federal fiscal and economic policies and pay increase guidelines. It also lets the Commission define terms, delegate some authority, and ask agencies for needed information.

11636.s: This order sets rules for employee-management relations in the Foreign Service. It gives Foreign Service employees the right to form, join, or help organizations, while limiting that right for management officials and confidential employees in some cases. It also creates procedures for recognizing employee organizations, consulting on personnel policies, and appealing some management decisions.

11637.s: This order adjusts basic pay rates for the General Schedule, certain Veterans' Administration medical positions, and Foreign Service officers and staff. It also tells the Civil Service Commission, the Veterans' Administration, and the Department of State to set rules for converting pay to the new rates. The changes take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 1972.

11635.s: This order continues the Souris-Red-Rainy River Basins Commission beyond its current end date. The Commission will keep carrying out joint federal-state planning and coordination on water and related land resources. It is set to end on June 30, 1973, unless it is extended with the needed recommendations.

11634.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It adds the Chairman of the Pay Board and the Chairman of the Price Commission to level IV. It also removes two listed positions from level V and renumbers the remaining items in that section.

11633.s: The order directs the Secretary of Defense to set up a program for security clearance certificates for United States citizens who are directly employed by NATO, SEATO, or CENTO. It allows those certificates to be provided when the organizations request them, and it also provides for denial, revocation, or suspension of the certificates. The program applies to United States citizens working directly for the civil or military agencies of those organizations.

11632.s: This order adds a Rent Advisory Board. The President appoints its members and chooses its chairman. The board gives advice on stabilizing rents and helps the Commission by doing technical analyses of matters the Commission refers to it.

11631.s: This order makes certain income, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1960 to 1972 open to inspection during the Ninety-second Congress. The Committee on Public Works of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes, may inspect them for its investigation of how programs affecting the committee are administered. The inspection must follow Treasury rules on congressional review of tax returns.

11630.s: This order changes a previous executive order about economic stabilization. It lets each Pay Board member, except the chairman, name an alternate to serve when the member cannot attend a meeting. It also lets each Price Commission member, except the chairman, name an alternate for the same purpose.

11629.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to act for the President on adding other bird species to the list protected under the U.S.-Mexico migratory birds and game mammals convention. The Secretary of State must consult with the Secretary of the Interior when carrying out this authority.

11628.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the Environmental Protection Agency. The seal is described as a flower-like design with parts that represent the blue sky, green earth, blue-green water, and a white circle for the sun or moon. It applies to the Environmental Protection Agency.

11627.s: This order continues the Cost of Living Council and gives it broad authority to stabilize prices, rents, wages, and salaries. It creates a Pay Board and a Price Commission to help carry out that program, and it also establishes committees on interest and dividends, health services, and state and local government cooperation. The order keeps existing price and wage limits in place under the new program, except for raw agricultural products.

11626.s: This order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for the memory of Dean Acheson, a former Secretary of State. It applies to Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia and across the United States, its territories and possessions, and to U.S. embassies, legations, consular offices, other facilities abroad, and military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11625.s: This order directs the Secretary of Commerce to coordinate federal plans and programs that affect minority business enterprises. It also authorizes the Secretary to provide technical and management assistance, support pilot or demonstration projects, and set up an information center. A council made up of people knowledgeable in this field will advise the Secretary, and other federal departments and agencies must cooperate and report on their activities.

11624.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on Commerce, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, gift, and excise tax returns for the years 1939 to 1972. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation into the effects of organized criminal activity on interstate and foreign commerce. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11623.s: This order lets the Director of Selective Service issue the rules and regulations needed to carry out the Military Selective Service Act. Before new rules are issued, the Director must seek views from named officials, publish the proposal in the Federal Register, and follow the notice steps in the order. Existing presidential regulations stay in effect until the Director changes or revokes them. The order also says it does not take away the President’s own authority to waive requirements or issue rules under the Act.

11622.s: This order amends a prior executive order that created a board of inquiry. It adds the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, AFL-CIO, along with District Lodge 94 and Local Lodge 1484, and removes the name Morris L. Myers from the order. It affects the unions named in the order and the board of inquiry listing.

11621.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes between certain maritime employers and employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO, and the International Longshoremen's and Warehousemen's Union. The disputes involve steamship companies, stevedores, marine carpenters, lighterage operators, and other employers in related pier activities, and they affect ports on the Pacific, Atlantic, Great Lakes, and Gulf Coasts. The board is directed to report to the President by October 6, 1971.

11620.s: This order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff until interment as a mark of respect for the Honorable Hugo L. Black, former Associate Justice of the United States. It applies to Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the District of Columbia, throughout the United States and its territories and possessions, and to United States embassies, legations, consular offices, other facilities abroad, and military facilities and naval vessels and stations.

11619.s: This order exempts Rose A. Conway from mandatory retirement for an indefinite period of time. It affects her as the personal secretary of former President Truman and leaves the Civil Service Commission's authority under the civil service retirement law in place except as this order specifically exercises it.

11618.s: This order changes how the Government of the Ryukyu Islands is run. It says the legislative body will be a single house, with members directly elected by the people of the islands. It also says the Chief Executive will be elected by the people, must receive at least one-fourth of the total votes cast, and will serve the same term as the legislative body. The legislative body must set the election rules, qualifications for Chief Executive, and procedures for special elections when there is a vacancy.

11617.s: This order changes Executive Order 11615 by adding the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to the list of officials named in section 2(b). It affects the officials who carry out the price, rent, wage, and salary stabilization order.

11616.s: This order amends rules on labor-management relations in the Federal service. It changes how labor organizations are recognized, how grievances and arbitration are handled, and when employees may use official time for union business. It also allows dues to be withheld from pay in some cases for labor organizations and for associations of management officials or supervisors.

11615.s: This order stabilizes prices, rents, wages, and salaries for 90 days at levels no higher than set in the order. It also requires sellers and employers to keep records showing the highest prices or rents charged during the set period, and it does not apply to raw agricultural products. The order establishes the Cost of Living Council and gives it power to issue rules, make exceptions, and gather information to carry out the order.

11614.s: This order establishes the National Business Council for Consumer Affairs. The Council is made up of a chairman, a vice chairman, and other representatives of business and industry appointed by the Secretary of Commerce. It advises the President and several federal agencies on consumer affairs programs, looks at current and possible consumer problems, and serves as a forum and liaison between business and government. It may also help the business community respond to legitimate consumer grievances and advise on federal, state, and local plans that affect business and industry.

11613.s: This order adds the Environmental Protection Agency to the membership lists of four river basin commissions. It also requires the EPA Administrator to appoint a member to each commission to represent the agency. The change affects the Pacific Northwest, Great Lakes, Souris-Red-Rainy, and New England river basin commissions.

11611.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 through 1971 open to inspection by the Committee on Internal Security of the House of Representatives, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules. It must follow the Treasury rules named in the order.

11612.s: This order requires each Federal department and agency to set up an occupational safety and health program for Federal employees. The program must include a responsible official, safety policies and procedures, workplace inspections, ways to track injuries and illnesses, and reports to the Secretary of Labor. It also creates a Federal advisory council with representatives of Federal agencies and labor organizations to advise the Secretary. The Secretary of Labor must give guidance, evaluate agency programs, and submit an annual analysis to the President.

11610.s:
This order changes rules for government contracts tied to national defense functions. It lets some contracts include indemnification and hold harmless terms for unusually hazardous or nuclear risks, with approval by a senior military official and required notice and government control or help in claims or defenses.

It also changes a rule about when defense officials may use authority under a 1966 law. Before using that authority, they must first find that reasonable efforts were made to include the required clause and that other sources of supply are not reasonably available.

11609.s: This order gives several presidential duties to other officials in the government, including the Administrator of General Services, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the heads of several departments and agencies. Many of the duties involve rules and approvals for travel, pay, housing, medical care, reimbursements, land transfers, and other administrative matters. It affects federal employees, uniformed service members, veterans, and agencies that carry out these programs.

11608.s: This order abolishes the Federal Field Committee for Development Planning in Alaska. It also revokes earlier orders that dealt with that committee and directs the Secretary of Commerce to make the needed arrangements to end it.

11606.s: This order changes the Selective Service rules for how people are chosen for induction. It requires a random selection sequence to be set each year by a drawing in Washington, D.C., and used nationwide. The sequence is based on birthdays for registrants who turn 19 during the calendar year, and it stays in effect for each registrant while they remain subject to induction for military training and service.

11607.s: This order creates the Advisory Council on Intergovernmental Personnel Policy. The council is made up of up to 15 members appointed by the President, with members drawn mainly from Federal, State, and local governments, plus education and training groups, public employee or labor organizations, and the general public. It is to study and recommend ways to improve State and local public administration, train employees, strengthen personnel systems, and help move personnel between governments and schools.

11605.s: This order amends security rules for government jobs by expanding the kinds of group ties that can matter in determining eligibility. It covers knowing membership, affiliation, or sympathetic association with organizations described as totalitarian, fascist, communist, subversive, or linked to unlawful force or attempts to overthrow the government. It also revokes Executive Order 9835 and gives the Subversive Activities Control Board authority to hold hearings and make these group designations.

11603.s: This order transfers the Peace Corps to ACTION and gives the Director of ACTION many of the President’s functions under the Peace Corps Act and related rules. It also moves the National Voluntary Action Program to ACTION and lets the Director work on voluntary action programs, information, and grants when allowed by law. Some powers stay with the President, and the Secretary of State keeps control over international agreements and certain policy changes.

11604.s: This order changes a prior executive order that places certain federal positions in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It adds the Assistant to the Secretary for Health Policy at the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare to level IV. It also removes the Commissioner of the Water Quality Office at the Environmental Protection Agency from level V and renumbers the other items in that section.

11602.s: This order sets rules for federal contracts, grants, and loans so they support enforcement of the Clean Air Act. Federal agencies generally may not award contracts or assistance for work tied to a facility the Environmental Protection Agency has designated for certain Clean Air Act convictions. The order also lets the Administrator issue rules, lets agencies report possible violations, and allows limited exemptions and yearly reports to Congress.

11601.s: This order adds to the Secretary of Defense's delegated powers the President’s authority to suspend certain laws on the mandatory retirement or separation of Navy and Marine Corps officers. It applies during a war or a national emergency.

11600.s: The order approves an official seal for the Office of Management and Budget. The seal includes the Arms of the United States and wording that links the office to the Executive Office of the President of the United States. It applies to the Office of Management and Budget.

11599.s: The order creates a Special Action Office for Drug Abuse Prevention in the Executive Office of the President. The office is led by a director chosen by the President. The director is to coordinate federal drug abuse training, education, rehabilitation, research, treatment, and prevention programs, but not law enforcement activities or legal proceedings. The director also sets policies, develops plans, evaluates programs, and makes funding recommendations.

11598.s: The order directs the Secretary of Labor to require executive branch agencies to list suitable job openings with the State Employment Service or the United States Employment Service. It also requires some government contracts and subcontracts to include promises to list suitable openings with the state employment service system, to the maximum extent feasible. The order does not require agencies or employers to hire people referred by these offices, and it does not apply retroactively.

11597.s: This order changes Executive Order 11513 by raising the membership of the President's Commission on School Finance from sixteen to eighteen. It affects the commission's size and membership.

11596.s: This order designates the Customs Cooperation Council as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the council the privileges, exemptions, and immunities covered by that law, and does not reduce any other rights it may have from treaty or congressional action.

11595.s: This order amends a previous order to establish the Office of Consumer Affairs in the Executive Office of the President. It says the Office will be led by a Director and two Deputy Directors, all appointed by the President.

11594.s: This order directs government officers to use transportation priority and allocation powers to move people and goods needed for national defense, government functions, defense production, and public health and safety. It gives the Secretary of Transportation the job of setting the overall use of available transportation capacity, with help from the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness. It applies during the railroad strike and ends when rail service resumes, or after 15 days at most.

11592.s: This order gives the Director of the Office of Management and Budget the power to approve actions that the President could approve under the River and Harbor Act of 1970 and the Flood Control Act of 1970. Those approvals can be made without the President’s approval, ratification, or other action.

11591.s: This order amends part of Executive Order 11157. It changes one phrase by adding the words "duty or" before "leave" in section 403(ii).

11590.s: This order makes Executive Order 11222 apply to the United States Postal Service. It also makes Executive Order 11478 apply to the United States Postal Service and the Postal Rate Commission. These changes affect those two agencies under the Postal Reorganization Act of 1970.

11589.s: This order gives the United States Civil Service Commission the President’s authority to make rules for assignments to and from states under the Intergovernmental Personnel Act. It also gives the Commission authority over personnel standards on a merit basis under the Federal Civil Defense Act of 1950. If this part conflicts with a 1961 executive order, this order says the new rule controls.

11588.s: This order sets up a system to review wages, salaries, and prices in the construction industry. It creates a Construction Industry Stabilization Committee and craft dispute boards made up of labor, employers, and public members to decide whether proposed pay increases are acceptable. Federal agencies must also review federal and federally assisted construction projects and contracts to make sure they fit the order's criteria. The order affects construction workers, contractors, unions, and federal agencies.

11587.s: This order changes one listed federal position in the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It replaces "Commissioner, Federal Water Pollution Control Administration, Department of the Interior" with "Commissioner, Water Quality Office, Environmental Protection Agency."

11586.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for registrants ordered to report for induction. It says some registrants who are far from their local board may report at an Armed Forces Examining and Entrance Station, and if they are inducted or found not qualified, they do not have to follow the original order. It also rescinds one rule allowing certain registrants to request transfer for induction and makes other related changes to reporting and recordkeeping rules.

11584.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for 1950 through 1971 open to inspection during the Ninety-second Congress. The Senate Committee on Government Operations, or an authorized subcommittee, may inspect them for its study of government activities. The inspection must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11585.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between certain railroad carriers and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For thirty days after the report, the carriers and the employees may not change the working conditions involved in the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11583.s: This order creates the Office of Consumer Affairs in the Executive Office of the President and gives it a Director and Deputy Director appointed by the President. The office advises the President on consumer matters, coordinates federal consumer programs, and can review complaints and send them to the proper federal, state, local, or private group. It also sets up a Consumer Advisory Council to advise the Director and tells federal agencies to give due consideration to consumer interests when taking actions that affect products and services.

11582.s: This order sets rules for how federal agencies handle holidays for employees. It says when an employee is excused from work, how holiday workdays are counted, and how holidays are treated for pay and leave. It also applies to the Post Office Department and the United States Postal Service, except for the Postal Field Service. It revokes earlier orders on holiday observance by government agencies.

11580.s: This order approves a seal as the official seal of the National Credit Union Administration. It applies to the agency and sets the design of its seal.

11581.s: This order changes which federal positions are listed in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It removes the Deputy Administrator, Federal Highway Administration, from level IV and renumbers the remaining items there. It also adds the Deputy Administrator, Federal Railroad Administration, to level V.

11579.s: This order transfers obligations, assets, rights, and responsibilities from earlier related programs to the Overseas Private Investment Corporation. It also delegates certain presidential functions related to the Corporation to the Corporation itself, and one rules-making function to the Civil Service Commission. Money that was obligated but not spent under a repealed section of the Foreign Assistance Act is transferred to the Corporation. The order takes effect when the Corporation’s Board of Directors adopts bylaws.

11578.s: This order establishes the Ohio River Basin Commission under the Water Resources Planning Act. The commission covers parts of Kentucky, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia that are in the Ohio River drainage basin, excluding the Tennessee River drainage basin. Its members include a chairman, federal department and agency members, state members, and members from certain interstate agencies. The chairman must report to the President through the Water Resources Council.

11577.s: This order raises the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It applies to members of the uniformed services and takes effect January 1, 1971.

11576.s: This order adjusts rates of basic pay under the General Schedule, certain Veterans' Administration medical and surgery schedules, and Foreign Service salary schedules. It affects federal officers and employees in those pay systems, including certain positions in the Veterans' Administration, Foreign Service officers, and Foreign Service staff officers and employees. It also requires the Civil Service Commission, the Veterans' Administration, and the Department of State to set rules for converting pay to the new rates.

11575.s: This order sets who can use parts of the Disaster Relief Act of 1970. It keeps some powers with the President, gives other powers to the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness, and gives specific powers to the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Agriculture. It also says federal agencies must plan for major disasters and coordinates those plans through the Office of Emergency Preparedness. The order revokes three earlier executive orders.

11574.s: This order directs the executive branch to run a permit program to regulate the discharge of pollutants and other refuse into navigable waters of the United States and their tributaries, and the placing of such matter on their banks. The Secretary of the Army is responsible for issuing, denying, conditioning, revoking, or suspending these permits, after consulting with the Environmental Protection Agency and other agencies on water quality, fish and wildlife, and other environmental concerns. The Attorney General is to carry out the legal actions needed to enforce the Act and the permits.

11573.s: The order excused most employees of executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies from duty for one-half day on December 24, 1970. It did not apply to some employees of the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and others who needed to stay at their posts for national security or other public reasons, or whose absence would conflict with existing law. Agency heads were also told to use a liberal policy for annual leave over the holiday period for employees who want it.

11571.s: This order designates the Commissioner of the District of Columbia as the authority to carry out the District of Columbia Alley Dwelling Act. In that role, the Commissioner is to be known as the "National Capital Housing Authority." The Commissioner’s assistant or assistant for housing programs may act for the Commissioner, including during an absence, disability, or vacancy in the office.

11572.s: This order deals with the current railroad strike and the strain it puts on transportation of people and goods by rail. It directs government officers to use transportation priorities and allocations to move people and things needed for national defense, military requirements, government functions, defense production, and public health and safety. The Secretary of Transportation must determine the overall use of available transportation capacity and direct the use of transportation priorities. The order stays in effect until rail service resumes, but no longer than 15 days after the strike ends.

11570.s: This order puts the Postal Rate Commission under federal ethics rules for government officers and employees. It directs the Civil Service Commission to write conduct rules for commissioners and employees, including limits on conflicts of interest, ex parte contacts, and outside gifts or payments from people or groups that do business with the Commission. It also requires employees to file confidential statements about outside work and financial interests, and for the rules to be published in the Federal Register.

11569.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations. It adds a category of aliens who are not required to register if they were employed continuously for one year by a firm or related entity and enter the United States temporarily to keep working for the same employer in a managerial, executive, or specialized knowledge job. It also covers the spouse or minor child of such a person if they are accompanying or following to join them. These aliens must have a visa or other official document showing they entered under the listed immigration law provision.

11567.s: This order sets the pay for the Director of the Bureau of Domestic Commerce at the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule. It sets the pay for the Deputy Director at the highest rate for grade 18 of the General Schedule. It also replaces a 1962 presidential letter about the salary of the former Administrator of the Business and Defense Services Administration.

11568.s: This order exempts A. Everette Maclntyre, a member of the Federal Trade Commission, from compulsory retirement for age. It keeps him in that position until February 29, 1972.

11566.s: This order sets up a Consumer Product Information Coordinating Center at the General Services Administration. The center is to review federal documents with product information, make selected information public, and cut down on duplicate consumer product information in government publications. Federal agencies must share documents with the center and work with it, while the order protects information that is exempt from disclosure or includes trade secrets and other competitive information. It also starts a pilot program to turn selected technical procurement documents into information useful to public consumers.

11565.s: This order changes who serves on the Committee for the Preservation of the White House. It sets the committee’s members, names the Director of the National Park Service as chairman, lets the President appoint additional members, and says members serve without pay.

11564.s: This order transfers several oceanographic, meteorological, and data programs from the Departments of Defense and Transportation to the Secretary of Commerce. It also lets the Secretary of Commerce use related powers and authority needed to run those programs. Personnel, property, records, and available funds tied to those programs are to be moved to the Department of Commerce as directed by the Office of Management and Budget.

11563.s: This order amends the Selective Service regulations for how local boards respond to induction calls. It sets the order for selecting registrants, including volunteers, nonvolunteers, and certain age groups, and it creates rules for priority groups and deferred or postponed cases. It also allows some registrants to be ordered for induction even if they have not yet been found acceptable or sent a Statement of Acceptability in certain cases.

11562.s: This order directs the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare to develop and coordinate a national program for physical fitness and sports. It calls for work with citizens, groups, schools, State and local governments, and Federal agencies to improve fitness programs, research, and school health and physical education, including for children, youth, adults, the handicapped, and the physically underdeveloped. It also creates the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports and a Conference on Physical Fitness and Sports to advise the President and the Secretary.

11560.s: This order changes Executive Order 11508 by replacing one board member role with another. It removes the "Director of the Bureau of the Budget" and puts the "Associate Director of the Office of Management and Budget" in that place.

11561.s: This order delegates a presidential authority under the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964 to the Civil Service Commission and the Secretary of State. The Civil Service Commission gets that authority for laws it administers, and the Secretary of State gets it for the Foreign Service Act of 1946, as amended.

11558.s: This order creates a five-member board to investigate disputes between certain railroad carriers and some of their employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. Until then, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions at issue unless they agree to do so.

11559.s: This order creates a board of five members to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by three labor organizations. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. From the date of the order and for thirty days after the board reports, no change can be made in the conditions at issue unless the parties agree.

11557.s: This order changes the rules for the President's Commission for the Observance of the Twenty-Fifth Anniversary of the United Nations. It allows the Commission to have up to fifty members, including members from public or private life and members of the Senate and House of Representatives chosen by the President.

11556.s: This order puts the Director of the Office of Telecommunications Policy in charge of federal telecommunications policy and coordination. It gives the Director duties such as advising the President, working with agencies and Congress, planning for emergencies, and helping manage radio spectrum and frequency assignments. It also directs federal departments and agencies to cooperate with the Director, while keeping the Federal Communications Commission’s existing authority in place.

11555.s: This order changes the Selective Service regulations for local board members. It says they must be U.S. citizens who live in the county where the board has jurisdiction, cannot be in the armed forces or a reserve component, and must be at least 30 years old.

11554.s: This order suspends a rule that limited how many Navy officers below the appropriate promotion zone could be recommended for promotion. The suspension lasts for two years from the date of the order and affects Navy officers who may be recommended by a promotion board.

11553.s: This order changes Selective Service regulations for registrants in Class I-A, Class I-A-0, or Class I-0. It lets a local board order a registrant to appear for a medical interview if the board thinks the registrant has one or more disqualifying medical conditions or physical defects listed in the rules. It also revokes two paragraphs in that section of the regulations.

11552.s: This order directs the Secretary of State to lead and coordinate federal efforts to increase participation in international organizations by using details and transfers of qualified federal employees. It tells executive branch agencies to help by sharing job openings, allowing short leave for interviews, and giving assessments of employees who are being considered. It also gives some authority to the Civil Service Commission and the Secretary of State, and it revokes Executive Order No. 10804.

11551.s: This order changes an earlier executive order on the National Council on Indian Opportunity. It says the council will include the Vice President as chairman, several cabinet officials, the Director of the Office of Economic Opportunity, and eight Indian leaders appointed by the President for two-year terms. It affects the membership of the council.

11550.s: This order changes Executive Order 11248 by replacing one listed position in level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It deletes the title "Chief, Children's Bureau, Social and Rehabilitation Service, Department of Health, Education, and Welfare" and adds "Counselor to the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare" instead. It affects that position in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

11549.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 10361, which had established the Whittier Defensive Sea Area in Alaska. It affects that defensive sea area and the authority tied to it.

11548.s: This order gives parts of the President’s duties under the Federal Water Pollution Control Act to the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Transportation, the Federal Maritime Commission, the Council on Environmental Quality, and the Coast Guard. It covers work on oil and hazardous substance discharge rules, inspections, removal plans, reports, and related enforcement duties. It also says that when Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1970 takes effect, the Interior Secretary’s duties under this order will vest in the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, with some required consultations continuing.

11547.s: This order amends a previous executive order about coordinating youth opportunity programs. It keeps the President’s Council on Youth Opportunity and says the Vice President will serve as chairman. The council includes several cabinet officials and other federal officials the President may choose, and each member may appoint a delegate.

11545.s: This order creates a Defense Distinguished Service Medal, along with ribbons and other items, for award by the Secretary of Defense. It is for military officers who performed exceptionally meritorious service in a duty of great responsibility in certain Defense Department and joint military jobs. The medal can be awarded only once to a person, but a device may be added for later qualifying service, and it may be awarded after death.

11546.s: This order creates a President’s Commission to mark the United Nations’ twenty-fifth anniversary. The Commission is to look at matters important to the United Nations and United States participation in it, suggest new initiatives, and make recommendations to the President on U.S. policy. It is also to consult with government agencies and private organizations and report its conclusions and recommendations by April 30, 1971.

11544.s: This order creates a Vice Presidential Service Certificate and a Vice Presidential Service Badge for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who served in the Office of the Vice President for at least one year after January 20, 1969. The awards are given by service secretaries on the recommendation of the Military Assistant to the Vice President. The badge may be worn during and after the person’s assignment, and each award may be granted posthumously.

11542.s: This order changes one Federal Executive Salary Schedule position in the Department of Housing and Urban Development. It deletes the title "Director, Demonstration Cities Administration" and replaces it with "Deputy Assistant Secretary for Model Cities."

11543.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes except by agreement.

11541.s: This order delegates functions related to the Office of Management and Budget to its Director, under the President’s direction. It also says prior budget-related rules and actions stay in effect unless changed or revoked. The Domestic Council is assigned work on domestic needs, goals, priorities, program review, and policy advice to the President, and the Council for Urban Affairs, the Cabinet Committee on the Environment, and the Council for Rural Affairs are terminated, with their functions moved to the Domestic Council.

11540.s: This order amends a prior order that placed certain federal positions in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It changes one level IV title to "Assistant Director, Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President" and adds the "Associate Director, Office of Management and Budget, Executive Office of the President" to level IV. It also removes the "General Counsel, Office of the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations" from level V and renumbers two items there.

11538.s: This order gives the Secretary of Transportation the President’s authority to establish and conduct an International Aeronautical Exposition without further presidential approval. It directs each federal department and agency to cooperate with the Secretary and provide requested help within the law and available funds. It also lets the Secretary redelegate these functions within the department.

11539.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of State to negotiate agreements with foreign governments that limit the export of certain cattle, goat, and sheep meats and their import into the United States. It also authorizes the Secretary of Agriculture to issue regulations for how those meats may enter the country or be withdrawn from warehouse for consumption. Other agencies must provide information and take actions needed to carry out those agreements and regulations.

11536.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Campus Unrest. The commission must study dissent, disorder, and violence at colleges and universities and report its findings and recommendations to the President. It also must look for the causes of campus violence, ways to resolve grievances without force, and ways to protect academic freedom and peaceful dissent and protest.

11537.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for ordering some registrants for induction. It says that if a registrant in Class I-A or I-A-O refuses or fails to report for an armed forces physical examination, he may still be ordered to report for induction even if he has not been found acceptable for service yet. The physical examination would then be done after he reports, and he would not be inducted until his acceptability is determined.

11535.s: This order lets the House Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain tax returns and related records during the Ninety-first Congress. It covers income, excess-profits, estate, gift, unemployment, and excise tax returns. The committee can also get a copy of a return on request, under Treasury rules.

11534.s: This order creates a National Council on Organized Crime. The council is made up of senior officials from the Justice Department, Treasury, Labor, the FBI, the Secret Service, Customs, Immigration and Naturalization, and other federal offices. Its job is to make a national strategy for the elimination of organized crime and meet when called by the Attorney General.

11532.s: This order creates an Interdepartmental Committee to help promote the voluntary Payroll Savings Plan for buying United States Savings Bonds. The committee is made up of a chairman, a vice chairman, and the heads of federal agencies, and it must help set up the plan, solve problems, share information, and suggest improvements. Each federal agency must put the committee’s plan into use as soon as practicable for civilian and uniformed personnel.

11533.s: This order delegates the President’s powers under the Export Administration Act of 1969 to the Secretary of Commerce, who may redelegate them. It reestablishes a review board made up of the Secretaries of Commerce, State, and Defense to review certain export license matters involving national security or major policy issues. The Secretary of Commerce must report to the President, and existing export-related actions stay in effect until changed by proper authority.

11530.s: This order changes rules for Department of Agriculture personnel assigned abroad. It says they will also be covered by the rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of State, in addition to other allowances and benefits that already apply.

11531.s: This order gives the Attorney General the President’s power to name certain U.S. attorneys and U.S. marshals for training. It applies to people appointed by the President as United States Attorneys and United States Marshals.

11529.s: This order terminates the Interdepartmental Committee on Narcotics. It also terminates the President's Committee on Juvenile Delinquency and Youth Crime and the Citizens Advisory Council, and revokes the two executive orders that created them.

11528.s: This order changes the area covered by the New England River Basins Commission. It adds certain portions of Long Island Sound, part of Long Island in New York, and part of New York in the Housatonic River drainage area. It also adds a member from the Atomic Energy Commission to the Commission.

11527.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for deferments and physical exams. It updates who can be deferred for civilian work, approved schooling or training, agricultural work, and fatherhood, and it revokes some older deferment rules. It also lets registrants under age 26 ask in writing for one preinduction physical examination, with limits set by the local board and possible temporary suspension by the Director of Selective Service.

11525.s: This order adjusts upward the monthly basic pay for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. It says some people who became entitled to certain payments after December 31, 1969, but before the Federal Employees Salary Act of 1970 was enacted, will not get any increase in those payments from this order. It also gives the Secretary of Defense authority to prescribe other rules for retroactive compensation for the uniformed services.

11526.s: This order creates the National Council on Federal Disaster Assistance. The council helps coordinate federal disaster aid, advise the Office of Emergency Preparedness, and encourage cooperation with state and local governments and private groups. It also supports sharing information, rebuilding efforts, research on preventing disasters, and review of disaster assistance programs.

11524.s: This order adjusts pay rates for the General Schedule, Postal Field Service, Rural Carrier, Veterans’ Administration medicine and surgery, and Foreign Service pay schedules. It also tells the named agencies to write the rules for converting employees to the new rates. The order applies to officers and employees covered by those schedules.

11523.s:
This order creates the National Industrial Pollution Control Council. The council is made up of business and industry representatives appointed by the Secretary of Commerce, with a chairman, vice-chairman, and an executive director.

The council advises the President and the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality on industry programs related to environmental quality. It may review industry plans, examine environmental problems tied to industrial practices, encourage industry to improve the environment, and advise on federal, state, and local policies affecting industry.

11522.s: The order gives the Director of the United States Information Agency responsibility for emergency plans and preparedness programs for essential foreign information activities. It says the agency must be ready to keep those activities going during a national emergency, including an attack on the United States. It also requires plans for foreign information programs, emergency broadcasting and teletype, advice to the Executive Branch on foreign opinion, and support for psychological operations and military command.

11521.s: This order lets federal agencies make special "veterans readjustment appointments" for certain Vietnam era veterans and disabled veterans in competitive service jobs up to GS-5 or the equivalent. It applies to veterans who meet the education, qualification, and timing rules in the order. The appointments must be tied to an agency training or education program, and workers who do not meet the conditions can be removed.

11520.s: This order changes rules for the Presidential Service Certificate and the Presidential Service Badge. It reestablishes the certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who have been assigned to the White House Office or certain military units and support facilities for at least one year after January 20, 1969. It also replaces the White House Service Badge with the Presidential Service Badge for members of the Armed Forces assigned to those duties, and sets who may award and wear it.

11519.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to help restore and maintain postal service and to carry out postal laws. It allows the use of U.S. Armed Forces and calls any or all Army National Guard and Air National Guard units into active military service for this purpose. The order affects the Postal Service, the Department of Defense, and the National Guard units and members called up under it.

11518.s: This order tells the Small Business Administration to speak for small business concerns when they deal with federal departments and agencies. It also tells those departments and agencies to ask the Small Business Administration for advice when actions may affect small business well being, competitive strength, or chances to start, grow, or expand. The order says the agency should especially consider minority-owned small business concerns and members of minority groups seeking to enter business.

11517.s: This order lets the Secretary of State issue and sign warrants naming agents to receive people extradited by a foreign government and take them to their trial in the United States. The agents keep the powers given by U.S. treaties and law. It also amends an earlier executive order by deleting one paragraph and renumbering two others.

11516.s: This order changes Executive Order 11248, which places certain positions in level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It removes the position of Director, Office of Minority Business Enterprise, Department of Commerce, and replaces it with Assistant to the Secretary, Department of Commerce. This affects one Department of Commerce position in the federal executive salary system.

11515.s: This order terminates the Interdepartmental Highway Safety Board, the Interagency Committee on International Athletics, the President's Committee on Manpower, and a task force tied to the Ohio River Bridge collapse. It also revokes certain earlier executive orders and changes the Medal of Freedom order so the President may select any person recommended for the award or chosen on his own initiative. The Bureau of the Budget or other designated agencies are directed to wind up the remaining affairs of the terminated bodies.

11514.s: This order tells the Federal Government to lead efforts to protect and improve the quality of the environment. Federal agencies must review their policies, monitor their activities, share public information, and work with other government bodies on environmental matters. The Council on Environmental Quality is directed to review federal environmental policies, recommend changes, issue guidelines, and help coordinate federal programs.

11513.s: This order creates the President’s Commission on School Finance. The commission is to study future revenue needs and resources for public and non-public elementary and secondary schools and report its findings to the President. It also looks at school funding, tax bases, federal aid, school spending differences, and ways to improve the use of education funds and data.

11511.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about basic allowances for quarters for members without dependents. It deletes the words “at his permanent station” from one part of that order.

11512.s: This order tells the Administrator of General Services to plan, acquire, and manage federal office space and buildings in the United States. It requires the Administrator and executive agencies to use federal space efficiently, make the most of government-owned buildings, and consider factors like public access, working conditions, housing, parking, and local plans. Executive agencies must work with the Administrator, give early notice of changing space needs, and review ways to move services away from the District of Columbia when that can be done without excessive cost or major loss of efficiency.

11510.s: This order amends a prior executive order by changing one Department of Commerce position name. It deletes "Special Assistant for Regional Economic Coordination" and inserts "Special Assistant to the Secretary for Policy Development" in the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that Department of Commerce position.

11509.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Council on Management Improvement. The council has 10 members from outside the Government, and it advises the President on management problems, reviews government operations, and makes recommendations to improve efficiency and cost control. Federal agencies may be asked to provide information and staff help for the council's work.

11508.s: This order tells executive agencies to review the real property they control and report any property that is not used, underused, or not being put to its best use. It also tells the Administrator of General Services to set standards, survey federal real property holdings, and report property that should be listed as excess property. A Property Review Board is created to review those reports and make recommendations to the President about how the property should be used or disposed of.

11506.s: This order changes an earlier tax exclusion for acquisitions of certain original or new Japanese stock or debt obligations. After the effective date, the exclusion no longer applies to acquisitions of those debt obligations. It still applies to stock acquired by converting a debt obligation issued before the effective date, if no additional payment is made.

11507.s: This order tells federal agencies to design, operate, and maintain their facilities to meet air and water quality standards. It requires agencies to prevent or reduce pollution, handle wastes safely, and prepare plans for existing and new federal facilities. It also requires water resources projects to be reviewed for their effects on water quality.

11505.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on the Judiciary, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1960 to 1969. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the administration, operation, and enforcement of the Internal Security Act of 1950 and other internal security laws, and it must follow Treasury rules.

11504.s: This order amends a previous executive order that places certain positions in level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It changes one listed Defense position from "Assistant to the Deputy Secretary of Defense" to "Assistant to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense."

11503.s: This order excuses most federal employees from duty on Friday, December 26, 1969, the day after Christmas Day. It also says that day is a holiday for federal employee pay and leave rules. Agency heads may still require some employees to work for national security or other public reasons, and they are told to use a liberal policy for annual leave over the holiday period.

11502.s: This order changes the rules for the President’s Committee on the National Medal of Science. It increases the number of ex officio members from one to two and names the President’s Science Adviser and the President of the National Academy of Sciences as those members.

11500.s: This order changes a section of Executive Order 11452 about the Council for Urban Affairs. It expands the list of people who may be directed to serve, adding “others” to the heads of departments and agencies the President may direct.

11501.s: This order delegates many presidential duties under the Foreign Military Sales Act to the Secretaries of State and Defense. It keeps the Secretary of State responsible for the general supervision of sales, including whether a sale is negotiated, concluded, or ended. It also says the Secretaries of State and Defense must consult with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Administrator of the Agency for International Development, and the Director of the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency on matters tied to their duties.

11499.s: This order changes a prior executive order on the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It removes the position of Assistant Archivist, Office of Presidential Libraries, General Services Administration, and adds the Commissioner, Transportation and Communications Service, General Services Administration instead.

11498.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the power to approve regulations about early discharge of regular enlisted members of the armed forces. It applies to regulations issued by the Secretaries concerned under section 1171 of title 10 of the United States Code.

11497.s: This order changes Selective Service rules to use a random selection sequence for induction. It applies nationwide to registrants and sets how men in different age and service categories are chosen for induction. It also changes the order local boards use when filling induction calls, including rules for delinquents, volunteers, and men whose random number has already been reached.

11495.s: This order assigns many Disaster Relief Act duties to the Director of the Office of Emergency Preparedness. It lets that office handle funds for road and highway repair, grants for damaged timber and debris removal, temporary housing, assistance for unemployed people, and grants and loans for fire suppression. It also gives the Secretary of Agriculture the role of deciding when food coupons and surplus commodities should be distributed after a major disaster.

11496.s: This order sets a rule on certain meat from Honduras for the rest of 1969. It stops fresh, chilled, or frozen cattle meat, and fresh, chilled, or frozen meat of goats and sheep except lambs, from being entered into the United States or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption. The order does not apply to meat released before the order took effect under a separate tariff law provision.

11493.s: This order establishes the Council for Rural Affairs and puts the President in charge of its meetings. The council includes several Cabinet officials and other federal leaders. It advises the President on policies for rural and non-metropolitan areas, helps find problems in rural America, and works to coordinate federal programs and public services in those areas.

11494.s: This order establishes the Presidential Citizens Medal and its ribbons. It is for U.S. citizens who have done exemplary service for their country or fellow citizens. The President may award it at his or her discretion, and it may also be awarded after a person has died.

11491.s: This order sets rules for labor-management relations in the Federal executive branch. It gives federal employees the right to form, join, help, or leave a labor organization, and it tells agencies not to interfere with that choice. It also creates a council and a panel to oversee the order, handle disputes, and set regulations. The order does not apply to the FBI, the CIA, and some other agencies or offices in certain cases.

11492.s: This order amends a prior order to establish the Citizens Advisory Committee on Physical Fitness and Sports. The President may appoint the committee’s members, designate its chairman, and the committee meets when the chairman calls it.

11489.s: This order changes one Treasury Department position listed in the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It replaces the title "Special Assistant to the Secretary (for Enforcement)" with "Special Assistant to the Secretary (Congressional Relations)."

11490.s: This order assigns emergency preparedness duties to federal departments and agencies. It requires them to plan for continuity of government, protect essential records and personnel, and be ready to carry out essential functions in a national emergency. It also gives specific emergency planning tasks to departments like State, Treasury, and Defense. The order says these plans can be carried out only if Congress or the President gives authority to do so.
