11488.s: This order includes a tract of land in Carter County, Tennessee, as part of the Cherokee National Forest. The land is about 15.1 acres and is transferred under the terms of an agreement between the Tennessee Valley Authority and the United States Department of Agriculture. The transfer is subject to existing road rights and an electric power transmission line easement.

11487.s: This order sets who can act as Secretary of the Interior when the Secretary and Under Secretary are not available because of absence, disability, or vacancy. It allows certain Assistant Secretaries or the Solicitor of the Department of the Interior to fill in, in the order the Secretary may prescribe. If no order of succession is in place, they serve in the order they took office.

11486.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between certain rail carriers and some of their employees. It says the board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. It also says the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes, except by agreement, during that time and for thirty days after the report is made.

11485.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense control over the Army National Guard and Air National Guard of the District of Columbia while they are in militia status. It also lets the Secretary of Defense command their military operations and, under the President’s direction, order them out to aid District civil authorities. The Attorney General must advise the President on legal options and help set law enforcement policies if the National Guard is used to aid civil authorities.

11484.s: This order designates the United International Bureaux for the Protection of Intellectual Property, or BIRPI, as a public international organization. It gives BIRPI the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities BIRPI may already have or later get by treaty or congressional action.

11483.s: This order makes income tax returns for the years 1960 to 1970 open to inspection by the House Select Committee on Crime, or a subcommittee it authorizes, during the Ninety-first Congress. The committee may use the returns for its study and investigation of crime in the United States. The inspection must follow rules set by the Secretary of the Treasury.

11482.s: This order establishes a Construction Industry Collective Bargaining Commission to study and address collective bargaining problems in the construction industry. The commission includes members from the public, labor organizations, and employers, and it may make recommendations, hold hearings, and help mediate disputes. It may intercede in disputes that could significantly affect construction activity, but it is not meant to require compulsory arbitration or limit the right to strike or lock out.

11481.s: This order directs that the U.S. flag be flown at half-staff on the day of Everett McKinley Dirksen’s interment. It applies to federal buildings, grounds, naval vessels, and U.S. offices and facilities abroad, including military facilities.

11480.s: This order sets up the President's Committee on Employment of the Handicapped and an Advisory Council to support it. The committee is directed to help create more employment opportunities for physically handicapped, mentally retarded, and mentally restored people by sharing information, educating the public, and working with employers and government agencies. It also replaces earlier orders on this subject and transfers the old committee’s members, records, property, funds, and pending business to the new committee.

11478.s: This order says the federal government must provide equal opportunity in federal employment and forbid discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. It requires each executive department and agency to set up and maintain an affirmative equal employment program for civilian employees and job applicants. The Civil Service Commission must guide these programs, review agency progress, and handle discrimination complaints with a fair review and appeal process. The order also applies to certain military, legislative, judicial, and District of Columbia positions, but not to aliens employed outside the United States.

11479.s: This order directs that the United States flag be flown at half-staff on Federal Government buildings, grounds, and naval vessels in the metropolitan area of the District of Columbia. It applies from the day of death until interment, in memory of Everett McKinley Dirksen, a former Senate minority leader and member of the Senate.

11477.s: This order lets the Atomic Energy Commission make certain awards without approval from the President. The Commission may give up to five awards in a calendar year, and each award cannot be more than $5,000, for especially meritorious contributions to the development, use, or control of atomic energy.

11476.s:
This order prescribes the "Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1969 (Revised edition)" for the armed forces. It applies to court-martial processes on and after August 1, 1969.

It also says ongoing investigations, trials already started, and other actions begun before that date may continue under the rules that were already in place. The order says it does not make punishable any act that was not punishable before August 1, 1969, and it limits punishment for offenses committed before that date to the limit then in effect.

11474.s: This order adjusts basic pay and salaries for several groups of federal workers. It changes the General Schedule, Postal Field Service, Rural Carrier Schedule, certain positions in the Veterans’ Administration Department of Medicine and Surgery, and Foreign Service officers and staff. It also sets rules for how affected employees are moved to the new pay rates.

11475.s: This order adjusts upward the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. The new pay rates take effect on July 1, 1969.

11472.s: This order creates the Environmental Quality Council and the Citizens' Advisory Committee on Environmental Quality. The Council advises and assists the President on environmental quality matters, reviews federal plans and actions affecting outdoor recreation and natural beauty, and helps coordinate work across federal agencies. The Committee advises the President and the Council on matters assigned to the Council. The order also ends the President's Council on Recreation and Natural Beauty and the older advisory committee on that subject.

11473.s: This order changes the rules for incentive pay for hazardous duty involving flight operations on the flight deck of an aircraft carrier. It applies to certain members of the crew of a fixed-wing aircraft carrier or an aviation unit operating from that type of carrier who are designated and ordered to that duty. It says they must meet set flight deck participation requirements in a month to qualify, and they cannot get this pay if they are also eligible for other hazardous duty pay for that month or part of a month.

11471.s: This order sets up how the United States will carry out the Convention on the Service Abroad of Judicial and Extrajudicial Documents in Civil or Commercial Matters. It designates the Department of State as the Central Authority to receive requests for service from other Contracting States. It also names the Department of State, the Department of Justice, and the United States Marshal or Deputy Marshal in the district where service is made as authorities that may complete the required certificate.

11470.s: This order creates a national voluntary action program within the executive branch to encourage more widespread voluntary action to solve public domestic problems. It also sets up a Cabinet Committee on Voluntary Action to advise and help the President and to coordinate work across federal departments and agencies. The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development is given duties related to urban living and poverty, including a clearinghouse for information and seed money grants for innovative private voluntary action programs.

11468.s: This order changes which federal jobs are placed in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It removes the Executive Director, Cabinet Committee on Price Stability from level IV and puts the Deputy Under Secretary for International Labor Affairs, Department of Labor in that slot instead. It also adds the Deputy Assistant Postmaster General, Bureau of Operations, Post Office Department, and the Director, Office of Minority Business Enterprise, Department of Commerce, to level V.

11469.s: This order changes the rule for when the National Commission on the Causes and Prevention of Violence ends. The Commission will terminate after it submits its final report or on December 10, 1969, whichever comes first.

11467.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s authority to accept or reject recommendations from the International North Pacific Fisheries Commission. It also gives the Secretary of State authority to approve or reject actions of the International Pacific Halibut Commission. The Secretary of State must consult with the Secretary of the Interior when carrying out this authority.

11466.s: This order lets the Director of the Bureau of the Budget choose projects for joint funding under two federal laws. The Director may also name one federal agency to run a jointly funded project for all the agencies involved. A designated agency may waive some technical grant or contract rules, but not if the waiver would change the project or lacks agreement from the agency that set the rule and provided the funds.

11465.s: This order says certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1950 to 1969 may be inspected by the House Committee on Internal Security or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for investigations allowed under House rules. It must follow Treasury rules for congressional inspection of tax returns.

11464.s: This order changes the tax rates on certain purchases of stock of foreign issuers and debt obligations of foreign obligors by United States persons. It lowers the stock tax rate to 11.25 percent of actual value and sets new debt tax rates based on time left until maturity. The changes apply to acquisitions made after April 4, 1969, with a trade-date rule for exchange-traded transactions.

11463.s: This order adds the General Counsel of the Office of the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that specific position in the federal government.

11462.s: This order closes most executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on Monday, March 31, 1969, as a mark of respect for Dwight David Eisenhower. It does not apply to offices and installations that agency heads decide should stay open for national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also lets agency heads excuse certain employees from duty on Friday, March 28, 1969, without charging leave.

11460.s: This order creates the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board. The board advises the President on foreign intelligence work, reviews intelligence activities by the CIA and other agencies, and reports its findings and recommendations. Its members are appointed from outside the government, and Executive Order 10938 is revoked.

11461.s: This order makes income, estate, and gift tax returns for 1956 to 1970 open to inspection by the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes, during the Ninety-first Congress. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the policies, procedures, and practices in the administration of the Federal-Aid Highway Program. The inspection must follow Treasury rules on how congressional committees may inspect tax returns.

11459.s: This order gives the Secretary of Transportation authority to approve and certify containers and vehicles for international transport of goods under customs seal. It also lets the Secretary issue regulations, set a fee schedule to cover the cost of these services, and delegate some of this authority. The order applies to containers, vehicles, and the nonprofit firms or associations the Secretary may authorize.

11458.s: This order directs the Secretary of Commerce to coordinate federal plans and programs that affect minority business enterprise and to help gather and share information about it. It also tells the Secretary to work with state and local governments, businesses, universities, foundations, and other groups to support minority business enterprises. The order creates an Advisory Council for Minority Enterprise to advise the Secretary, and it asks other federal departments and agencies to provide information and assistance when requested.

11457.s: This order makes certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns open to inspection by the House Committee on Government Operations, or an authorized subcommittee. It applies to returns for the years 1947 to 1970 during the Ninety-first Congress and must follow Treasury rules for inspecting returns.

11456.s: This order creates a Special Assistant to the President for Liaison with Former Presidents in the White House Office. The Special Assistant is to keep living former Presidents informed on matters the President wants shared and to pass along their views to the President on issues of current interest. The order also tells certain federal departments and agencies to provide information and other help when asked.

11455.s: This order creates the Office of Intergovernmental Relations and places it under the Vice President. The Vice President is made the President’s liaison with State and local officials and is directed to help improve cooperation between Federal, State, and local governments. The Office is also told to handle Federal-State-local problems, track recurring issues, and review how Federal agencies let State and local officials comment on assistance programs and other intergovernmental matters.

11454.s: This order lets the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1948 through 1969. The inspection is for the committee’s study of government activities and must follow Treasury rules for congressional review of tax returns.

11453.s: This order creates the Cabinet Committee on Economic Policy and says the President will lead its meetings, with the Vice President leading when the President is absent. The committee includes several cabinet and White House officials, and the President may add other department or agency heads. It is meant to advise and assist the President on national economic programs and policies, help set goals and strategy, promote coordination of Federal economic programs, and consult with academic, agricultural, business, consumer, and labor groups.

11452.s: This order establishes the Council for Urban Affairs and puts the President in charge of its meetings. The Council includes the Vice President and several cabinet officials, and the President may add other department or agency heads. It advises and assists the President on urban affairs, helps develop a national urban policy, promotes coordination of federal programs in urban areas, and encourages cooperation among federal, state, and city governments.

11451.s: The order creates the President's Commission on Personnel Interchange. The Commission is to develop a program that places promising young executives from federal departments and agencies and the private sector in challenging jobs in the other sector. It also is to develop an education program, review the program, and advise the President on ways to promote interchange between government and the private sector. Federal departments and agencies must cooperate, name a liaison, and the Civil Service Commission must provide administrative support.

11450.s: This order designates the Secretary of the Treasury to take the actions required of the United States under a part of the Customs Convention on the International Transport of Goods Under Cover of TIR Carnets. It also allows the Secretary to delegate and subdelegate that authority as he thinks appropriate.

11449.s: This order sets out how the United States will take part in the International Coffee Agreement. It gives certain duties to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Secretaries of Agriculture, Commerce, and Labor, while keeping other duties with the President. It also says the work must be coordinated among federal agencies and lets each Secretary redelegate those duties within their department. The order keeps one earlier order in force with an update and revokes another earlier order.

11448.s: This order establishes a Meritorious Service Medal, along with ribbons and other appurtenances, for members of the armed forces of the United States. It may be awarded for outstanding meritorious achievement or service to the United States, under regulations set by the proper military authorities. No more than one medal may be awarded to one person, but a suitable device may be given for later qualifying achievements or service. The medal or device may also be awarded after death and given to an appropriate representative of the deceased.

11446.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation to set rules for accepting medals and ribbons offered by multilateral organizations other than the United Nations. It applies to members of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, and Coast Guard when it is not operating as part of the Navy. A decision to allow acceptance must have the concurrence of the Secretary of State.

11445.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain railroad employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen. The board must report its findings to the President. During the period set by the order, the carriers and their employees may not make changes in the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11447.s: This order appoints the listed federal officials to the Interagency Advisory Committee on Compensation for Motor Vehicle Losses. It also allows each member to name an alternate to attend Committee meetings when they cannot go.

11444.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the listed rail carriers and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that time, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions out of which the disputes arose except by agreement.

11443.s:
This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the carriers listed in the order and certain employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days.

From the date of the order and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11442.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between the Long Island Rail Road and certain employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report, the rail road and its employees cannot change the working conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to it.

11441.s: This order changes a prior executive order to place certain federal positions in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It adds the Director of the United States Secret Service to level IV, changes the level V listing from Director to Deputy Director of the Secret Service, and adds the Assistant Archivist in the Office of Presidential Libraries to level V.

11440.s: The order directs executive departments and agencies to work with the Administrator of General Services when they plan exhibits and displays for their programs. It says they should make these materials in a way that can also support later exhibition as part of the archival and cultural heritage of the United States. After the materials have served their main program purpose, they may be transferred to the Administrator, who can arrange for exhibition, preserve them, or dispose of them.

11439.s: This order revokes Executive Order No. 11372, which had designated the Lake Ontario Claims Tribunal as a public international organization entitled to privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It applies to the Lake Ontario Claims Tribunal after the President found that it had discharged its functions and adjourned.

11437.s: This order suspends a section of federal law about service-in-grade requirements for promotion of officers in the Navy and Marine Corps. It also revokes three earlier executive orders.

11438.s: This order sets procedures for honorary recognition or cash awards to members of the armed forces for suggestions, inventions, or scientific achievements that improve government operations. The award can be recommended when another executive department or agency adopts or uses the idea, and it must be justified with documentation. A cash award for one idea cannot be more than $25,000. The cost is transferred from the department or agency that benefits to the Department of Defense or the Department of Transportation.

11435.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Interior power to accept a State’s return of some or all civil or criminal jurisdiction over Indian country. Acceptance must be published in the Federal Register and must name the jurisdiction returned and the date it takes effect. For criminal jurisdiction, the Secretary must first consult with the Attorney General.

11436.s: This order suspends part of section 6372 of title 10 of the United States Code. That section deals with the retirement or retention on the active list of certain rear admirals in the Navy. It affects those rear admirals covered by that section.

11434.s: The order tells the Secretary of State and the Director of the United States Information Agency to make policies and regulations for their Foreign Service personnel systems after consultation with other federal officials. It also gives the Board of the Foreign Service and the Board of Examiners more duties for Foreign Service information officers and other United States Information Agency personnel. The order delegates retirement and disability rulemaking for certain Foreign Service staff and amends an earlier order to add two United States Information Agency officials to the board.

11432.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Treasury the President’s functions over the import of arms, ammunition, implements of war, and related technical data. It says the Secretary of the Treasury must consult with other agencies and be guided by the Secretary of State on matters affecting world peace, U.S. external security, and foreign policy. It also keeps existing import-control rules in effect under the Treasury Department and transfers pending import license applications from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of the Treasury.

11433.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the Illinois Central Railroad Company, Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, the companies and their employees may not change the conditions that led to the disputes except by agreement.

11431.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes between certain maritime employers and employees represented by the International Longshoremen's Association, AFL-CIO. The disputes involve steamship companies, stevedores, marine carpenters, lighterage operators, and others engaged in related pier activities. The board must report to the President by October 2, 1968, and then continue to carry out other duties under the law.

11430.s: This order prescribes a new Manual for Courts-Martial for the armed forces of the United States. It applies to court-martial processes started on or after January 1, 1969. It also says earlier investigations, trials, and other actions already begun may continue under the laws and rules that applied before, and it does not make punishable acts that were not punishable before that date.

11429.s: This order changes a travel expense rate in a previous executive order. It raises the mileage amount for claimants and beneficiaries of the Veteran's Administration and their attendants from five cents a mile to six cents a mile.

11428.s: This order ends the President's Advisory Committee on Supersonic Transport. It also revokes the earlier executive order that created the committee and the section that amended it.

11427.s: This order ends the Maritime Advisory Committee that was created by Executive Order 11156. It also revokes that earlier order.

11426.s: This order keeps the Director of the Office of Emergency Planning as the President’s liaison with the governors of the States and Territories. The office is to help handle Federal-State problems and serve as a clearing house for them. Federal departments, agencies, and regional boards are told to cooperate and help, and each department or agency head must designate a contact official if asked. The order does not give the director authority over other federal departments or agencies.

11425.s: This order directs the Special Representative for Trade Negotiations to study United States foreign trade policy and recommend needed legislative and other measures. It asks for views from members of Congress, several federal agencies, and a new Public Advisory Committee on Trade Policy. The committee is made up of no more than 35 members from outside the United States Government, and the order abolishes the earlier Public Advisory Committee for Trade Negotiations.

11424.s: This order changes the rules for incentive pay tied to hazardous duty involving aerial flight. It defines “aerial flight” as flight in an aircraft, glider, or spacecraft, from takeoff from the surface of the earth until the next full stop on the surface. It also defines “aviation accident” for a member who must often and regularly fly and is injured or disabled during certain flight-related incidents.

11423.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to receive and process applications for permits for certain facilities at the U.S. borders that connect with a foreign country. It covers pipelines, conveyor belts, water and sewage lines, monorails, aerial cable cars, aerial tramways, and some bridges. The Secretary of State must ask for views from other federal officials and may send a disputed application to the President for a final decision.

11422.s: This order sets a federal policy for cooperative planning and carrying out manpower training and support programs. It says several federal departments and agencies must take part in the Cooperative Area Manpower Planning System, or CAMPS, to help plan and run these programs in urban and rural areas. It also calls for coordination with state and local governments and nongovernment organizations, and says the Department of Labor will provide administrative support for the coordinating committees.

11421.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Reserve Affairs to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that Defense Department position and how it is listed in the federal salary system.

11420.s: This order sets up the Export Expansion Advisory Committee. The committee is made up of the Secretaries of Commerce, Treasury, and State, along with the President and Chairman of the Export-Import Bank. It reviews and makes recommendations on loans, guarantees, and insurance used to finance export expansion, and it gives guidance to the Bank on using those funds to support foreign trade and the long-term commercial interest of the United States.

11419.s: This order bars imports into the United States of commodities or products from Southern Rhodesia that were exported after May 29, 1968. It also prohibits many U.S.-related persons from helping sell, ship, finance, or carry Southern Rhodesian goods or funds, with limited exceptions for medical, educational, news, humanitarian, and certain food needs. The order also restricts U.S. air carriers and aircraft from traveling to or from Southern Rhodesia or operating in coordination with Southern Rhodesian aircraft.

11417.s: This order changes Executive Order 10973 by adding the Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Domestic and International Business to the Development Loan Committee. It affects the committee’s membership under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.

11418.s: This order changes an earlier order that created the President's Advisory Council on Cost Reduction. It replaces the council’s end date with May 24, 1969, so the council stays in place until then.

11416.s: This order adds the position of Assistant to the Deputy Secretary of Defense to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that Defense Department position by placing it in the schedule named in the order.

11414.s: This order raises the monthly basic pay rates for members of the uniformed services within each pay grade. The new rates take effect on July 1, 1968.

11413.s: This order adjusts basic pay rates for workers under the General Schedule and changes salary schedules for certain positions in the Veterans' Administration Department of Medicine and Surgery. It also adjusts pay for Foreign Service officers and for certain staff officers and employees in the Foreign Service. No salary rate may be paid above the rate for level V of the Executive Schedule.

11415.s: This order creates two advisory committees: one on selecting physicians, dentists, and allied specialists, and one on health resources. The committees share the same membership, appointed by the President from private life, and one member serves as chairman of both. They advise on selective service matters and on the allocation, use, and administration of health resources, including manpower, facilities, and emergency preparedness.

11412.s: This order creates a National Commission on the Causes and Prevention of Violence. The commission is told to investigate and make recommendations on the causes and prevention of violence, including assassination, murder, assault, disrespect for law and order, disrespect for public officials, and violent disruptions of public order. It also may look at other matters the President puts before it. The commission must report its findings and then end within the time set in the order.

11411.s: This order changes Executive Order 11394, which set up the President's Commission for the Observance of Human Rights Year 1968. It replaces the limit of "ten other members" with wording that lets the President appoint such other members from public or private life as he may choose.

11409.s: This order changes which federal jobs are placed in levels IV and V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It replaces some listed positions with others at the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare and adds two new positions to level IV. It also changes one level V position to Deputy Administrator, Health Services and Mental Health Administration.

11410.s: This order changes Executive Order 11183 by replacing one sentence in section 1. It says one member of the Commission will be chosen by the President to serve as Chairman.

11407.s: This order reestablishes the Presidential Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Coast Guard who have been assigned to the White House for at least one year. It also replaces the White House Service Badge with the Presidential Service Badge. The badge and certificate are awarded to military personnel assigned to duty in the White House under rules set by the named secretaries.

11405.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to disperse people engaged in acts of violence and to restore law and order in Maryland. It allows the use of Armed Forces of the United States if needed. It also authorizes calling Army National Guard and Air National Guard units or members into active military service for an indefinite period, with relief or recall at the Secretary of Defense’s discretion.

11406.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense, and any military department secretary he designates, use the President’s authority to order units in the Ready Reserve to active duty. It applies to units in an armed force and allows active duty for up to 24 months. This authority lasts until June 30, 1968.

11404.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to disperse people involved in the violence described in the proclamation and to restore law and order in Illinois. It allows the use of the Armed Forces of the United States if needed. It also authorizes calling Army National Guard and Air National Guard units or members into active military service until they are relieved.

11403.s: The order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to disperse people engaged in violence in the Washington metropolitan area and to restore law and order. It also directs protection of federal property, personnel, and functions, as well as embassies of foreign governments and international organizations. The Secretary of Defense may use the Armed Forces and may call Army National Guard and Air National Guard units or members into active military service.

11402.s: This order changes the President's Council on Recreation and Natural Beauty and makes the Vice President its chairman. It lists several Cabinet and agency leaders as council members, and each may appoint a delegate to take part in council work. When the council considers matters that affect other federal agencies, the chairman must invite those agency heads to join the talks.

11400.s: This order adds the position of Special Assistant for Regional Economic Coordination in the Department of Commerce to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position and the salary schedule for executive jobs.

11401.s: This order designates the Commissioner of the District of Columbia as the authority to carry out the District of Columbia Alley Dwelling Act. It says the Commissioner will be known as the "National Capital Housing Authority" when carrying out those duties. The Assistant to the Commissioner may act for the Commissioner as directed, and will act as the authority if the Commissioner is absent, disabled, or if the office is vacant.

11399.s: The order creates the National Council on Indian Opportunity. The Council includes several federal officials and six Indian leaders appointed by the President. It is meant to encourage the use of federal programs for the Indian population, coordinate agency work, review those programs, and suggest improvements.

11398.s: This order establishes the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports and a Citizens Advisory Committee. The Council is to develop policies to improve physical fitness and sports participation for Americans, including children, youth, adults, and school pupils with handicaps or physical underdevelopment. It also calls for better coordination of federal programs, cooperation with state and local governments, and research in physical fitness and sports performance.

11397.s: This order lets agency heads make a "transitional appointment" for certain veterans and disabled veterans who served during the Vietnam era, if they are qualified and have less than one year of education beyond high school. The appointee must do satisfactory work and complete required education or training, or be removed. Those who meet the conditions and finish a year of current continuous service can be changed to career-conditional or career employment.

11396.s: This order designates the Attorney General to coordinate Federal criminal law enforcement activities and crime prevention programs. It also covers Federal programs meant to help State and local law enforcement agencies and crime prevention efforts. Every Federal department and agency must cooperate with the Attorney General and provide reports, information, and assistance when requested, within the law and available funds.

11395.s: This order changes how the Chief Executive of the Ryukyu Islands is chosen. It says the Chief Executive will be elected by the people of the Ryukyu Islands on the same day as the legislative body, and that the legislative body must set election rules, qualifications, and special elections for vacancies. If a new Chief Executive is not chosen within a reasonable time, the High Commissioner may appoint one until a successor is elected.

11393.s: This order changes a prior executive order by replacing item (6) with the position of Deputy Director of Defense Research and Engineering, Department of Defense. It affects how that position is listed in the Federal Executive Salary Schedule.

11392.s: This order calls certain units of the Ready Reserve in the Naval Reserve, Air Force Reserve, and Air National Guard into active duty. The service units listed include tactical fighter, tactical reconnaissance, military airlift, rescue, attack, and fighter squadrons and groups. Their active duty period is for not more than 24 months.

11394.s: This order creates the President's Commission for the Observance of Human Rights Year 1968. The Commission is made up of several Cabinet members, other federal officials, and ten members appointed by the President. It is to promote observance of 1968 as the 20th anniversary of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights, study and report on progress, and work with federal, state, local, educational, civic, labor, and other groups.

11391.s: This order amends Selective Service rules for registrants outside the United States. It says certain registration, classification, and notice forms must be mailed directly to registrants at military post offices, Canada, or Mexico, and other foreign addresses must go through the Director of Selective Service. It also says some registrants outside the United States must return the Classification Questionnaire through the Director within 60 days unless the local board gives more time.

11390.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense, and certain military department officials the Secretary designates, the power to carry out several presidential functions without further approval from the President. The functions include matters about Army and Air Force officers, chaplains, uniforms, enlisted training rules, reserve officer promotions, and some Navy and Marine Corps retirement and band matters. It also keeps earlier presidential actions on these matters in effect unless they are changed or revoked under this order.

11389.s: This order adds the Director of the Office of Foreign Direct Investments in the Department of Commerce to the list of positions in level IV of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position and changes how it is classified under the salary schedule.

11388.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Department of Commerce when the Secretary and Under Secretary are not available because of absence, disability, or a vacancy. In that case, an Assistant Secretary of Commerce or the General Counsel of the department will act as Secretary, following the order set by the Secretary or, if none is set, the order in which they took office. It also replaces Executive Order No. 10148.

11386.s: This order directs the Secretary of Commerce to coordinate federal regional economic development work and keep liaison with regional commissions and the Alaska field committee. It also establishes the Federal Advisory Council on Regional Economic Development, made up of several federal officials and federal cochairmen. The order requires federal departments and agencies involved to cooperate and keep the Secretary and the Council informed of their regional development plans. It also changes prior orders related to Alaska and Appalachia.

11387.s: This order limits certain transfers of capital to or within foreign countries by people in the United States who own or acquire at least a 10% interest in a foreign business venture, unless the Secretary of Commerce authorizes it. It also lets the Secretary of Commerce require some of those people to bring back to the United States certain earnings, bank deposits, and other short-term financial assets held abroad, and they must comply. The Board may also investigate, regulate, or prohibit similar transactions by banks and other financial institutions, and may require them to repatriate some foreign-held short-term financial assets.

11385.s: This order adds the Deputy Administrator of the Federal Highway Administration in the Department of Transportation to level IV of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects the pay level for that position.

11384.s: This order adds the Director of the United States Secret Service in the Treasury Department to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position.

11383.s: This order allows the Senate Select Committee on Standards and Conduct, and any authorized subcommittee, to inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1948 to 1968. The inspection is for its investigation of allegations that members, officers, or employees of the Senate engaged in improper conduct, broke the law, or violated Senate rules while doing their duties. The inspections must follow Treasury rules on access to tax returns.

11381.s: This order changes the makeup of the Federal Council for Science and Technology. It says the council will include the President’s Special Assistant for Science and Technology and one representative from each listed federal department, agency, and foundation. It also allows a representative of the Director of the Bureau of the Budget to attend meetings as an observer.

11382.s: This order changes several earlier executive orders to put transportation-related duties under the Secretary of Transportation and, in some cases, the Federal Aviation Administrator. It covers matters like classified information, airport law, life saving medals, contracting, claims, international aviation, highway safety, supersonic transport, wartime status, Alaska development committees, and Coast Guard functions. It also says certain prior actions stay in effect unless changed later, and it revokes four earlier executive orders.

11379.s: This order sets who will serve as Commissioner of the District of Columbia if the Commissioner is absent, disabled, or the office becomes vacant. The Assistant to the Commissioner would act first, and the Corporation Counsel would act next.

11380.s: This order changes earlier rules on mutual educational and cultural exchange. It lets certain government agencies handle reports and some receipts and leasing matters under those exchange programs. It also approves regulations that allow U.S. government employees stationed in foreign countries to be given living quarters, including heat, fuel, and light, in government-owned or rented buildings without cost to them.

11378.s: This order exempts Daniel J. Quill, the Postmaster at San Antonio, Texas, from compulsory retirement for age. The exemption lasts for three years and affects Mr. Quill under the Civil Service Retirement Law.

11377.s: This order directs the United States Tariff Commission to keep reviewing whiskbrooms and other brooms listed in the tariff schedules. It must report each year to the President on the estimated annual consumption of those brooms and explain the basis for its estimates. Starting with the 1968 report and every two years after that, it must also report on the production of and trade in other brooms it finds competitive, and if possible estimate their annual consumption.

11376.s: This order changes the membership of the President's Council on Aging. It replaces the list of council members with certain cabinet officials and federal leaders, and makes one of them the chairman.

11375.s: This order amends earlier equal employment rules to add sex to the kinds of discrimination barred in federal employment and in employment by federal contractors and subcontractors. It requires federal agencies and the Civil Service Commission to handle complaints of discrimination on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. It also requires contractors to take affirmative action, post notices, and state in job ads that qualified applicants will be considered without regard to those traits.

11373.s: This order transfers certain property, records, assets, and liabilities from the National Capital Transportation Agency to the Washington Metropolitan Area Transit Authority. It also gives the Director of the Bureau of the Budget authority to carry out the transfer and to handle the unexpended balance of appropriations and other funds of the Agency. The records transferred do not include records relating to individual employees or officers.

11374.s: This order abolishes the Missile Sites Labor Commission and moves its functions and responsibilities to the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service. It also transfers the commission’s records and property, and says disputes already before the commission will be handled by its former members under special assignment. The order directs federal agencies, manufacturers, contractors, construction concerns, and labor unions to keep cooperating to avoid labor disputes and work stoppages at missile and space sites.

11371.s: This order establishes the New England River Basins Commission. Its jurisdiction covers the six New England states and part of New York, with some areas in Vermont and Massachusetts excluded. The Commission includes a chairman, members from certain federal departments and agencies, members from the listed states, and members from interstate agencies with jurisdiction in the area. The chairman must refer certain international matters to the Council and report to the President through the Council.

11372.s: This order designates the Lake Ontario Claims Tribunal as a public international organization. It gives the tribunal the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act.

11370.s: This order allows the House Committee on Public Works, or a subcommittee it authorizes, to inspect certain income, estate, and gift tax returns from 1956 through 1968. The inspection is for the committee’s investigation of the policies, procedures, and practices used in administering the Federal-Aid Highway Program. The inspection must follow Treasury rules for viewing congressional returns.

11369.s: This order adds two jobs to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects the Administrator of the Social and Rehabilitation Service and the Chief of the Children’s Bureau in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

11368.s: This order changes the interest equalization tax rates for United States persons who buy stock of foreign issuers or debt obligations of foreign obligors. It sets a 18.75 percent tax rate for stock and sets different tax rates for debt obligations based on how long they have left until maturity. It also amends an earlier order so certain Japanese debt obligations, and stock received when converting those debt obligations, are exempt from the tax under stated conditions.

11367.s: This order changes Executive Order 11248 by adding the position of Assistant Director for Executive Management in the Bureau of the Budget in the Executive Office of the President. It affects the federal executive salary schedule by placing that position in level IV.

11366.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense authority to order some members of the Ready Reserve to active duty. It applies to people who are not serving satisfactorily in a Ready Reserve unit, have not finished their reserve obligation, and have not served 24 months on active duty. It also lets the Secretary extend a member’s service until the required active duty time is reached, and it applies similar authority to Ready Reserve members of the Coast Guard when it is not operating as part of the Navy.

11365.s: This order creates a National Advisory Commission on Civil Disorders. The commission is to investigate the causes of recent major civil disorders in cities and recommend ways to prevent or control them, including better communication, law enforcement training, and coordination between local, state, and federal authorities. It may also study other matters the President places before it, and it must issue an interim report and a final report before it ends.

11364.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to take steps to disperse people engaged in violence and restore law and order in Michigan. It authorizes the use of the Armed Forces of the United States if needed. It also allows the Secretary of Defense to call Army National Guard and Air National Guard units of Michigan into active military service for an indefinite period until relieved.

11363.s: The order designates the International Secretariat for Volunteer Service as a public international organization. It gives the group the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act.

11362.s: This order directs the government to use transportation priorities and allocations during the railroad strike. It says these powers should be used to move people and goods needed for national defense, including military requirements, government functions, defense production, and public health and safety. The Secretary of Transportation is directed to set the overall use of available transportation capacity and to manage the priority system.

11361.s: This order suspends a rule about the service-in-grade requirement for Marine Corps officers who are first lieutenants. It affects their eligibility to be considered by a selection board for promotion to the next higher grade.

11360.s: This order amends Selective Service rules and updates several terms used in the regulations. It changes who is exempt from registration, who may serve on appeal boards and local boards, and how certain appeal agents may be assigned. It also revises draft classification rules for conscientious objectors, students, people in military reserve service, and some people in needed occupations or graduate study.

11359-A.s: This order changes a prior executive order that set up the President's Council and Committee on Recreation and Natural Beauty. It adds the Secretary of Transportation to the council's membership list and includes that office in the council's makeup.

11359.s: This order establishes the Souris-Red-Rainy River Basins Commission. The commission’s area covers parts of Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota that are drained by the Souris-Red-Rainy Rivers system. It includes a chairman, federal members, state members, and members from certain interstate agencies, and it is expected to consult with Montana on matters affecting the small headwater drainage in that state. The chairman must also refer international matters to the Water Resources Council, and the commission is set to end under the order’s stated conditions unless it is extended.

11358.s: This order lets the House Committee on Un-American Activities, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns for the years 1948 to 1967. The inspection is for investigations of subversive and un-American activities and propaganda. It must follow Treasury rules on how congressional committees may inspect tax returns.

11357.s: This order says the National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act of 1966 will be carried out through the National Highway Safety Bureau and its director. It affects the bureau and the director responsible for carrying out that law.

11356.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the listed rail carriers and certain employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen. The board must report its findings to the President within 30 days. From the date of the order and for 30 days after the report is made, the carriers and their employees may not change the conditions behind the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11354.s: This order changes how presidential proclamations are prepared and handled. It adds a required closing statement for proclamations and says signed orders or proclamations must be sent to the Director of the Office of the Federal Register for publication. It also changes when the Seal of the United States applies to presidential documents and says one older order does not apply to proclamations except those for treaties and other international agreements.

11355.s: This order changes a prior executive order on appointments under the Defense Production Act of 1950. It requires the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission to survey certain appointments and changes the kind of statistical report that must be made about those appointments. It also revokes Part II of Executive Order No. 10647.

11353.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Council on Cost Reduction. The council is directed to review government cost reduction efforts, advise the President on ways to improve them, and look for cost-saving practices in government, business, and industry. It may also ask executive departments and agencies for information and assistance, and it must submit a final report to the President.

11351.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about the European Space Research Organization being treated as a public international organization. It adds a paragraph saying that earlier order is effective as of May 31, 1966. It affects the legal status and effective date of that organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act.

11350.s: This order changes Selective Service rules for registrants, local boards, appeal boards, and government appeal agents. It sets or restates deadlines for requests to appear, appeals, and appeals to the President. It also changes the process for conscientious objector cases and for handling medical and induction records for registrants found qualified or not qualified for service.

11352.s: This order suspends a part of federal law about Marine Corps officers who hold the rank of lieutenant colonel. It affects their service-in-grade requirement for being considered by a selection board for promotion to the next higher grade.

11349.s: This order amends an earlier order on consumer interests and creates the President's Committee on Consumer Interests. The committee studies federal agency programs that affect consumers and makes recommendations to the President, and it may advise agencies on how their plans affect consumer matters. It also creates a Consumer Advisory Council to advise the President and the committee on consumer interest issues.

11347.s: This order changes the membership of the Temporary Commission on Pennsylvania Avenue. It lists the officials who make up the Commission and says the Chairman shall invite the Architect of the Capitol to be a member. The order also allows the President to appoint other members.

11346.s: This order adds the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Mortgage Credit at the Department of Housing and Urban Development to level V of the Federal Salary Schedule. It changes the pay level for that one position.

11344.s: This order creates a board to look into a labor dispute between Avco Corporation and some of its employees at the Lycoming Division Plant in Stratford, Connecticut. The order says the dispute could lead to a strike that might affect part of the military aircraft industry and military aircraft engine industry and could imperil national safety. The board must report to the President and then stay in existence to do other tasks allowed under the law.

11345.s: This order establishes the Great Lakes Basin Commission under the Water Resources Planning Act. Its jurisdiction covers parts of Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin that are drained by the St. Lawrence River system, including the Great Lakes and related tributaries. The commission includes a chairman appointed by the President, members from certain federal departments and agencies, members from those eight states, and members from interstate agencies with approved compacts in the area.

11343.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between The Long Island Rail Road and certain of its employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, The Long Island Rail Road and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes unless they agree to do so.

11341.s: This order creates the President’s Commission on Postal Organization. The Commission is directed to study the organization and structure of the United States postal service and report on whether it should be transferred from the Post Office Department to a Government corporation or another form of organization. It is also to make recommendations on postal rates, compensation, personnel policies, financing, facilities, equipment, and mail handling. Executive departments and agencies may provide the Commission with information and assistance, and the Commission must submit its final report to the President within one year.

11340.s: This order sets April 1, 1967, as the date the Department of Transportation Act takes effect. It affects the Department of Transportation Act and the people and agencies that would operate under it.

11342.s: This order establishes the Quetico-Superior Committee. The committee is made up of members appointed by the President and members designated by the Secretaries of Agriculture and the Interior. It is directed to promote protection of the primitive quality of the Quetico-Superior canoe country and to advise and consult with U.S. and Minnesota officials.

11339.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s power to set the components and quantities of Army and Air Force rations, without needing further presidential action. It also lets the Secretaries of the Army and Air Force, under Defense Department rules, set special allowances and special or supplemental rations for their services. The order revokes several earlier executive orders on the same subject.

11338.s: This order adds the Deputy Under Secretary in the Department of Transportation to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It changes the pay level for that federal position.

11336.s: This order gives the Secretary of Agriculture power to act on emergency livestock feed help without needing the President’s approval in certain cases. It applies when a severe drought, flood, hurricane, blizzard, or other uncontrollable catastrophe increases hardship for needy members of an Indian tribe on reservation or other Indian land used for grazing livestock. The Secretary must work with the Secretary of the Interior, and the help ends when the Secretary of Agriculture gives notice.

11337.s: This order opens certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns from 1948 through 1966 to inspection by the Senate Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes. The inspection is for the committee’s studies of how government activities work at all levels and how to make government more economical and efficient. It must follow the Treasury Department rules named in the order.

11335.s: This order adds the Commissioner of the Property Management and Disposal Service at the General Services Administration to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that one federal position and changes where it fits in the executive pay schedule.

11334.s: This order designates the Asian Development Bank as a public international organization that can receive the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this does not change any privileges or immunities the bank may have under treaty or congressional action, or the applicability of Article 50 of the agreement establishing the bank. The order also changes earlier rules so the Council and the Secretary of the Treasury must handle the Asian Development Bank the same way they handle other international financial institutions.

11333.s: This order suspends part of section 6374 of title 10 for certain Marine Corps brigadier generals. It applies only to a brigadier general on the active list whose second failure to be selected for promotion to major general happened in the same fiscal year as the first failure.

11332.s: This order lets the House Committee on Government Operations, or a subcommittee it authorizes, inspect certain income, excess-profits, estate, and gift tax returns. It covers returns for the years 1947 through 1968 during the Ninetieth Congress. The inspections must follow Treasury rules for viewing congressional tax returns.

11330.s: The order sets up a federal council and a citizens advisory board on youth opportunity. It directs federal agencies to coordinate youth programs and improve planning, evaluation, and help for youth, especially disadvantaged youth. It also covers programs for education, employment, recreation, health services, and other activities for young people.

11331.s: This order establishes the Pacific Northwest River Basins Commission under the Water Resources Planning Act. The Commission’s area covers Washington, most of Oregon, and parts of Idaho, Montana, and Wyoming in the Columbia River drainage. It includes members from federal departments, those five states, certain interstate agencies, and the Chairman of the United States Entity for the Columbia River Treaty. The order also calls for consultation with California, Nevada, and Utah on matters that may affect small headwater drainages in those states.

11329.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between shipbuilding and repair companies and some of their employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, AFL-CIO. It says the dispute has led to a strike that could affect a substantial part of those industries and may imperil national safety. The Board is directed to report to the President and may keep working after the report is submitted if needed under the law.

11328.s: This order changes how the interest equalization tax applies to commercial banks that acquire debt obligations of foreign obligors. It says some tax exclusions will still apply to those bank acquisitions, but one exclusion applies only to purchases made by a commercial bank at branches outside the United States. It also lets the Secretary of the Treasury issue rules and require reports to carry out the order.

11326.s: This order extends parts of the Federal Aviation Act to the Ryukyu Islands for civil air transportation that starts, ends, or passes through the islands. It also requires the Civil Aeronautics Board to get and consider the High Commissioner’s views before acting on certain applications. The High Commissioner is told to control and regulate aviation in the Ryukyu Islands, except where this order says otherwise. It also removes the Ryukyu Islands from another executive order.

11325.s: This order sets rules for parole of people convicted of violating the Universal Military Training and Service Act or its regulations. It allows the Attorney General, on recommendation from the Director of Selective Service, to parole some people for induction into the Armed Forces, for noncombatant service, or for civilian work contributing to the national health, safety, or interest. It also explains how local boards, the Attorney General, and other officials handle applications, induction, reclassification, and what happens if a parolee is not inducted or is later discharged.

11327.s: This order lets the Secretary of Defense, and some military department secretaries, order certain Ready Reserve members to active duty. It applies to members who are not in a Ready Reserve unit or not participating satisfactorily, who have not finished their reserve obligation, and who have not served on active duty or active duty for training for a total of twenty-four months. It also allows their service to be extended until that total is reached, and says family responsibilities and work tied to national health, safety, or interest should be considered.

11324.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate disputes between the National Railway Labor Conference carriers and certain railroad employees. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. For that period, and for thirty days after the report, the carriers and employees may not change the conditions tied to the disputes except by agreement.

11323.s: This order adds the Deputy Commissioner of Social Security in the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that specific federal position.

11321.s: The order says there is a labor dispute between Union Carbide Corporation and some of its employees represented by the United Steelworkers of America at a plant in Kokomo, Indiana. It says the strike could affect a substantial part of the military aircraft engine industry and could imperil national safety. The order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into the dispute and report to the President.

11320.s: This order gives the Secretary of State, and the Under Secretary of State if designated, the power to make rules and regulations under the Foreign Gifts and Decorations Act of 1966. They may do this without approval from the President, and the rules must be published in the Federal Register.

11322.s: This order bars the import of certain goods from Southern Rhodesia, including asbestos, iron ore, chrome, pig-iron, sugar, tobacco, copper, meat and meat products, and hides, skins, and leather. It also prohibits U.S.-subject persons from helping export those goods, shipping them in U.S.-registered vessels or aircraft, or dealing in them in certain ways. The order further blocks activities involving arms, military equipment, aircraft, motor vehicles, and oil or oil products sent to Southern Rhodesia. It assigns enforcement duties to the Secretaries of State, Commerce, and the Treasury.

11318.s: This order designates the European Space Research Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives ESRO and its personnel certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities in the United States, including tax exemptions, customs relief, and immunity from some legal process. It also lets ESRO contract, own property, and bring legal proceedings in the United States.

11319.s: This order changes the design of the United States Coast Guard seal. It sets out the colors, words, and symbols to be used on the seal, including the motto "SEMPER PARATUS" and the words "UNITED STATES COAST GUARD 1790." It affects the Coast Guard and its official seal.

11317.s: This order changes the military punishment table for Article 113, which covers misbehavior of a sentinel or lookout. It sets different maximum punishments depending on whether the offense happens in an area designated for special pay for duty subject to hostile fire or in all other places. The punishments listed include dishonorable discharge, forfeiture of all pay and allowances, and confinement at hard labor.

11316.s: This order amends a prior executive order to add the Director of the Demonstration Cities Administration in the Department of Housing and Urban Development to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position and how it is classified for salary purposes.

11314.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into labor disputes between General Electric and certain of its employees. It covers the strike at the Evendale, Ohio, plant and threatened strikes at other General Electric plants. The order says these disputes may affect the military jet engine, military aircraft, military armament, and military electronics industries, and that they may imperil national safety.

11315.s: This order creates an executive assignment system for positions in grades GS-16, GS-17, and GS-18 in the Executive Branch. It sets rules for filling those jobs with career, limited, or noncareer assignments, and says selections must be based on merit and fitness in most cases. It also lets the Civil Service Commission approve, review, and revoke these assignments and requires agencies to work with the Commission on staffing.

11313.s: This order sets the line of succession for the office of Postmaster General. If that office is vacant, or if the Postmaster General is absent or disabled, the Deputy Postmaster General will act in that role. If neither is available, an Assistant Postmaster General or the General Counsel of the Post Office Department will act as Postmaster General in the order set out in the order. It also replaces earlier executive orders on this same subject.

11312.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the President’s functions under the Act about certain objects of cultural significance brought into the United States for temporary display or exhibition. The Secretary of State may decide whether a work of art or other object is of cultural significance and whether its temporary display in the United States is in the national interest. The Secretary of State may also publish public notices of those decisions and may delegate these functions within the Department of State.

11310.s: This order assigns the Attorney General emergency preparedness duties for law-enforcement functions in the federal government. It calls for emergency plans, training, legal advice, liaison with courts and Congress, and plans for controlling entry and departure, alien property, and security standards during an emergency. It also covers support for civil defense, including local law enforcement, prisons, and helping identify the dead and reunite families.

11311.s: This order says changes to the Tariff Schedules of the United States apply to articles entered or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption on and after January 1, 1967. It also designates the United States Information Agency to carry out the 1948 agreement on visual and auditory materials and to make the needed decisions and regulations.

11309.s: This order changes Executive Order 11215, which created the President's Commission on the Patent System. It replaces the words "18 months" with "20 months" in the section on the commission's work.

11308.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways and certain employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report, Pan American World Airways and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute except by agreement.

11307.s: This order directs the Secretary of Agriculture to lead coordination of Federal programs that affect agricultural and rural area development. It tells Federal departments and agencies to share information and work with the Secretary to avoid duplication, improve cooperation, and help with planning and technical assistance for State and local governments. It also says the order does not change the legal authority of any department or agency, and it replaces Executive Order 11122.

11305.s: This order gives the Secretary of the Army and the Governor of the Canal Zone authority over many Canal Zone matters. The Secretary of the Army is assigned powers over harbor and vessel rules, aircraft rules, health and quarantine rules, medical licenses, certain taxes, alcohol rules, and some entry and detention rules. The Governor is assigned powers over roads and vehicles, agreements with Panama about road use and taxes, postal savings interest, vessel operator licenses, magistrates' courts, and police power rules, subject to the limits in the order. It also keeps earlier actions and regulations in effect unless they are changed or revoked under this order.

11306.s: This order creates the President's Committee on Rural Poverty and the National Advisory Commission on Rural Poverty. The Committee is to review programs and policies affecting rural people and make recommendations to the Government and private enterprise. The Commission is to study rural economic conditions, make its own recommendations, and report to the Committee, and both bodies end ninety days after the Commission's final report is submitted.

11303.s: This order changes a prior executive order about transferring personnel to public international organizations. It waives a leave-of-absence limit for Reginald C. Price and treats him as having been on leave from March 9, 1954, through September 12, 1957. This is for the rights and benefits provided by the earlier executive order.

11304.s: This order amends the rules so the interest equalization tax does not apply to certain stock or debt obligations of Canada, if they are part of an original or new issue and the required notice is filed. It does not apply to certain investment company shares or to certain Canadian companies, partnerships, or trusts formed mainly to buy foreign securities. The same rules also apply to commercial banks, and the Secretary of the Treasury may issue rules to carry out the order.

11302.s: This order lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs pay travel costs for claimants and beneficiaries traveling to or from a Veterans' Administration facility or other place for vocational rehabilitation, counseling, examination, treatment, or care. It allows payment of actual travel expenses, or instead a mileage allowance of up to five cents a mile, plus ferry, bridge, road, and tunnel tolls. It also allows the travel expenses of an attendant to be paid in the same way, and some of these costs can be paid before travel is finished.

11301.s: This order creates the President's Committee on Libraries and the National Advisory Commission on Libraries. The Committee and Commission are directed to study the role of libraries, review policies and funding, and make recommendations for government and private action. The Commission must report to the Committee, and federal departments and agencies may be asked for information and help.

11300.s: This order names the Attorney General of the United States, and other Executive Branch officers and employees he chooses, as the United States’ “local authorities” and “competent officers” under Article XIII of the Convention with Greece. It directs them to carry out the obligations the United States assumed under that article in the way the Convention requires.

11299.s: This order adds the Director of the Urban Transportation Administration in the Department of Housing and Urban Development to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It changes the salary level for that federal position.

11298.s: This order sets the interest rate on savings deposits made by members of the uniformed services under Section 1035 of Title 10. Their deposits will earn 10 percent interest a year, compounded quarterly, starting September 1, 1966.

11296.s: This order directs executive agencies to consider flood hazards when planning new federal buildings, roads, and other facilities. It also tells agencies that give federal grants, loans, or mortgage insurance to avoid using flood plains when possible. Agencies that dispose of federal land or manage land use planning must also take flood hazards into account and may add use restrictions to land sales.

11297.s: This order tells the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to bring Federal departments and agencies together to work on programs that affect urban areas. It calls for meetings, shared information, and working groups to help coordinate Federal actions and avoid duplication. It also says agencies with urban programs must take part and give information when asked, to the extent allowed by law and available funds.

11295.s: This order gives the Secretary of State the power to make rules for granting, issuing, and verifying United States passports without further action by the President. It also supersedes two earlier executive orders about passports and foreign service regulations. Existing rules under those orders stay in effect until they are changed, revoked, or end by law.

11294.s: This order delegates the President’s authority to set maximum per diem allowances for civilian officers and employees of the Government when they are in travel status. It gives that authority to the Secretary of Defense for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone, and U.S. possessions, to the Secretary of State for areas outside the United States and those listed places, and to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget for travel en route to, from, or between localities outside the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia.

11293.s: This order adds the Commissioner of the Federal Water Pollution Control Administration in the Department of the Interior to level V of the Federal Executive Salary Schedule. It affects that federal position by placing it in the listed salary level.

11292.s: This order changes rules for incentive pay for hazardous duty and special pay for sea duty for enlisted members of the armed forces. It sets minimum aerial flight requirements for members on active duty and reserve components to qualify for incentive pay. It also says enlisted members may get additional pay for certain periods of duty aboard more than one vessel, at more than one designated place, or both, and it limits when sea-duty pay can be received with other pay or subsistence credit.

11291.s: The order creates a three-member board to investigate a dispute between American Airlines and certain employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO. The board must report its findings to the President within thirty days. During that time, and for thirty days after the report is made, American Airlines and its employees may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

11290.s: This order changes a prior order that delegated certain presidential functions to the Director of the Bureau of the Budget. It covers rules for civilian officers and employees who are transferred from one official station to another for permanent duty.
